data.v: ततो दुर्योधनो राजा साम्ना परमवल्गुना । तानाभाष्य महेष्वासान्प्राप्तकालमभाषत ॥
data.md: Thereupon king Duryodhana addressed these mighty bowmen in the most agreeable and pleasant terms and spoke them in a way most suited to the time.

data.v: मतिं मतिमतां श्रेष्ठाः सर्वे प्रब्रूत माचिरम् । एवं गते तु यत्कार्यं भवेत्कार्यकरं नृपाः ॥
data.md: Duryodhana said O monarchs, all of you are the best of the intellectual persons; do you at once give your individual opinions as to what is necessary or what is unnecessary under the present circumstances.

data.v: एवमुक्ते नरेन्द्रेण नरसिंहा युयुत्सवः । चक्रुर्नानाविधाश्चेष्टाः सिंहासनगतास्तदा ॥
data.md: Sanjaya said When these words had been uttered by the lord of men, then the foremost of princes, who had seated themselves on the throne and were most willing to fight, began to make various gestures (expressive of their heroism).

data.v: तेषां निशम्येङ्गितानि युद्धे प्राणाञ्जुहूषताम् । समुद्वीक्ष्य मुखं राज्ञो बालार्कसमवर्चसः । आचार्यपुत्रो मेधावी वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यमाददे ॥
data.md: Having understood the gestures of those, who were ready to sacrifice their lives in the battle and having beheld the face of the king, that had the splendour of the newly rising Sun. The highly intellectual son of Acharya, who

data.v: रागो योगस्तथा दाक्ष्यं नयश्चेत्यर्थसाधकाः । उपायाः पण्डितैः प्रोक्ताः सर्वे दैवसमाश्रिताः ॥
data.md: 'Zeal, perseverance, as also skillfulness and diplomacy, these have been declared by the learned me to be the principal expedients of accomplishing ends, which, again, are wholly dependent upon Destiny.'

data.v: लोकप्रवीरा येऽस्माकं देवकल्पा महारथाः । नीतिमन्तस्तथा युक्ता दक्षा रक्ताश्च ते हताः ॥
data.md: Those foremost of men, the mighty carwarriors, on our side, who had been like the celestials and who were acquainted with the principles of government were all slain in battle. In spite of all these, there should be no disappointment as regards victory.

data.v: न त्वेव कार्यं नैराश्यमस्माभिर्विजयं प्रति । सुनीतैरिह सर्वार्थैर्दैवमप्यनुलोम्यते ॥
ते वयं प्रवरं नॄणां सर्वैर्गुणगणैर्युतम् । कर्णं सेनापतिं कृत्वा प्रमथिष्यामहे रिपून् ॥
data.md: For, Destiny could be made favourable, if we can take recourse to the honest principles comprehensive of all the expedients. O descendant of the Bharata race, we shall, therefore, install Karna, that best of men, endowed with all the good qualities, as the commander of the army. Having made Karna the commander of our force, we shall be in a position to destroy all the enemies.

data.v: ततो दुर्योधनः प्रीतः प्रियं श्रुत्वा वचस्तदा । प्रीतिसंस्कारसंयुक्तं तथ्यमात्महितं शुभम् ॥
स्वं मनः समवस्थाप्य बाहुवीर्यमुपाश्रितः । दुर्योधनो महाराज राधेयमिदमब्रवीत् ॥
कर्ण जानामि ते वीर्यं सौहृदं च परं मयि । तथापि त्वां महाबाहो प्रवक्ष्यामि हितं वचः ॥
data.md: O Karna, I know your strength, as well as great intimacy that you entertain for myself. In spite of all that, O mighty-armed one, I will tell you some words that are beneficial to yourself.

data.v: श्रुत्वा यथेष्टं च कुरु वीर यत्तव रोचते । भवान्प्राज्ञतमो नित्यं मम चैव परा गतिः ॥
data.md: O hero, you are the greatest sage are always my highest protection as well. Now, having heard my words, do whatever you desire, or whatever you like most.

data.v: भीष्मद्रोणावतिरथौ हतौ सेनापती मम । सेनापतिर्भवानस्तु ताभ्यां द्रविणवत्तरः ॥
data.md: My two great generalissimos, Bhishma and Drona, those car-warriors of the first class, have been already slain in battle. You are more powerful than either of them. Now should you be installed as the commander of my army.

data.v: वृद्धौ च तौ महेष्वासौ सापेक्षौ च धनंजये । मानितौ च मया वीरौ राधेय वचनात्तव ॥
data.md: Indeed, those two mighty bowmen were very old; and they were favourable disposed and you towards Dhananjaya. In despite thereof, O son of Radha, those two heroes were selected by me as the generalissimo of my army at your word.

data.v: पितामहत्वं संप्रेक्ष्य पाण्डुपुत्रा महारणे । रक्षितास्तात भीष्मेण दिवसानि दशैव ह ॥
data.md: Beholding their connection of grand-father with themselves, the sons of Pandu, O father, were saved in that formidable battle by Bhishma for ten consecutive days.

data.v: न्यस्तशस्त्रे च भवति हतो भीष्मः पितामहः । शिखण्डिनं पुरस्कृत्य फल्गुनेन महाहवे ॥
data.md: When you had laid aside your arms, Bhishma of mighty prowess was slain in battle by Falguna, who had placed Shikhandin in his front.

data.v: हते तस्मिन्महाभागे शरतल्पगते तदा । त्वयोक्ते पुरुषव्याघ्र द्रोणो ह्यासीत्पुरःसरः ॥
data.md: When that great bowman had fallen and lain down on the bed of arrows, it was them, O foremost of men, that Drona was appointed as the commander (of the army) at your request.

data.v: तेनापि रक्षिताः पार्थाः शिष्यत्वादिह संयुगे । स चापि निहतो वृद्धो धृष्टद्युम्नेन सत्वरम् ॥
data.md: My opinion is, that by that hero, too, the sons of Pritha were saved (from the hand of Death) in consideration that the latter were the pupils of the former. But even that old man, again, was speedily slain (in battle) by Dhristadyumna.

data.v: निहताभ्यां प्रधानाभ्यां ताभ्याममितविक्रम । त्वत्समं समरे योधं नान्यं पश्यामि चिन्तयन् ॥
data.md: Reflecting for a while, I do not see any other person, like yourself, of more immeasurable prowess than those two best of warriors, who are already slain in battle.

data.v: भवानेव तु नः शक्तो विजयाय न संशयः । पूर्वं मध्ये च पश्चाच्च तवैव विदितं हि तत् ॥
data.md: At present you are able to obtain victory for ourselves. There is no doubt about it. In accordance therewith you have rendered good to us both before and after, as well as in the middle.

data.v: स भवान्धुर्यवत्संख्ये धुरमुद्वोढुमर्हसि । अभिषेचय सेनान्ये स्वयमात्मानमात्मना ॥
data.md: You should, like the commander of the force, bear all the burden in battle. So, should you be installed as the general by yourself.

data.v: देवतानां यथा स्कन्दः सेनानीः प्रभुरव्ययः । तथा भवानिमां सेनां धार्तराष्ट्रीं बिभर्तु मे । जहि शत्रुगणान्सर्वान्महेन्द्र इव दानवान् ॥
data.md: Therefore, do you maintain this force of Dhritarashtra, even as lord Skanda of eternal energy, the leader of the celestials, maintain the celestial force.

data.v: अवस्थितं रणे ज्ञात्वा पाण्डवास्त्वां महारथम् । द्रविष्यन्ति सपाञ्चाला विष्णुं दृष्ट्वेव दानवाः । तस्मात्त्वं पुरुषव्याघ्र प्रकर्षेथा महाचमूम् ॥
data.md: Do you slay all the foes, even as Mahendra slays the Danavas. When the most powerful car-warriors, the Pandavas, will see you waiting in the field of battle, they will surely fly away with all the Panchalas, even as the Danavas fly away, beholding Vishnu. Consequently, O foremost of men, do you command this mighty force.

data.v: भवत्यवस्थिते यत्ते पाण्डवा गतचेतसः । भविष्यन्ति सहामात्याः पाञ्चालैः सृञ्जयैः सह ॥
data.md: When you will stay in the field, all those Pandavas of wicked soul with their allies, the Panchalas and the Srinjayas, all will run away from the field.

data.v: यथा ह्यभ्युदितः सूर्यः प्रतपन्स्वेन तेजसा । व्यपोहति तमस्तीव्रं तथा शत्रून्व्यपोह नः ॥
data.md: So, do you exterminate all the enemies, even as the risen Sun, burning by his own energy, destroys the awful darkness.

data.v: उक्तमेतन्मया पूर्वं गान्धारे तव संनिधौ । जेष्यामि पाण्डवान्राजन्सपुत्रान्सजनार्दनान् ॥
data.md: Karna said O son of Gandhari, this was already told by me before you, namely that I would subdue all the Pandavas with their sons and with Janardana, too.

data.v: सेनापतिर्भविष्यामि तवाहं नात्र संशयः । स्थिरो भव महाराज जितान्विद्धि च पाण्डवान् ॥
data.md: I will be your generalissimo, there is not doubt about it. O powerful monarch, have peace. And do you think the Pandavas were already conquered.

data.v: एवमुक्तो महातेजास्ततो दुर्योधनो नृपः । उत्तस्थौ राजभिः सार्धं देवैरिव शतक्रतुः । सेनापत्येन सत्कर्तुं कर्णं स्कन्दमिवामराः ॥
data.md: Sanjaya said O great monarch, on his being thus addressed, king Duryodhana stood up with all other monarchs, like Indra of one hundred sacrifices with the celestials, in order to pay respect to Karna.

data.v: ततोऽभिषिषिचुस्तूर्णं विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा । दुर्योधनमुखा राजन्राजानो विजयैषिणः । शातकौम्भमयैः कुम्भैर्माहेयैश्चाभिमन्त्रितैः ॥
तोयपूर्णैर्विषाणैश्च द्वीपिखड्गमहर्षभैः । मणिमुक्तामयैश्चान्यैः पुण्यगन्धैस्तथौषधैः ॥
औदुम्बरे समासीनमासने क्षौमसंवृतम् । शास्त्रदृष्टेन विधिना संभारैश्च सुसंभृतैः ॥
जय पार्थान्सगोविन्दान्सानुगांस्त्वं महाहवे । इति तं बन्दिनः प्राहुर्द्विजाश्च भरतर्षभ ॥
जहि पार्थान्सपाञ्चालान्राधेय विजयाय नः । उद्यन्निव सदा भानुस्तमांस्युग्रैर्गभस्तिभिः ॥
data.md: O foremost of men, the bards and the twiceborn persons uttered these words to him-"Do you subdue the sons of Pritha, with Govinda and with their principal attendants in that formidable battle. O son of Radha, do you slay the sons of Pritha, along with the Panchalas, that we may win victory, even as risen Sun always destroys the thick gloom by his terrible rays.

data.v: न ह्यलं त्वद्विसृष्टानां शराणां ते सकेशवाः । कृतघ्नाः सूर्यरश्मीनां ज्वलतामिव दर्शने ॥
data.md: The faithless sons of Pandu with Keshava, cannot indeed bear with the sight of the arrows shot by you, even as it is most intolerable to look at the burning rays of the Sun.

data.v: न हि पार्थाः सपाञ्चालाः स्थातुं शक्तास्तवाग्रतः । आत्तशस्त्रस्य समरे महेन्द्रस्येव दानवाः ॥
data.md: Having put on all the weapons, the sons of Pritha, along with the Panchalas, will not be able to stay before you in the field, even as the Danavas are not able to stand before Indra (in battle).

data.v: अभिषिक्तस्तु राधेयः प्रभया सोऽमितप्रभः । व्यत्यरिच्यत रूपेण दिवाकर इवापरः ॥
data.md: Having been thus installed in the generalship, the son of Radha of unparalleled radiance surpassed all the beauty and splendour like a second Sun.

data.v: सेनापत्येन राधेयमभिषिच्य सुतस्तव । अमन्यत तदात्मानं कृतार्थं कालचोदितः ॥
data.md: Having installed the son of Radha in the leadership (of the army), thereupon, your son, insisted upon by Death as it were, considered himself most successful.

data.v: कर्णोऽपि राजन्संप्राप्य सेनापत्यमरिंदमः । योगमाज्ञापयामास सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति ॥
data.md: O monarch, Karna, the subduer of enemies, having obtained this leadership, ordered for arranging the troops in battle-array towards the rising of the Sun.

data.v: तव पुत्रैर्वृतः कर्णः शुशुभे तत्र भारत । देवैरिव यथा स्कन्दः संग्रामे तारकामये ॥
data.md: O descendant of the Bharata race, Karna, having been surrounded by your sons in the battle, looked resplendent, even as the lord Skanda, encompassed by all the celestials, looked radiant in the battle, wherein the Asura Taraka, like an evil, was sought to be defeated.

data.v: सेनापत्यं तु संप्राप्य कर्णो वैकर्तनस्तदा । तथोक्तश्च स्वयं राज्ञा स्निग्धं भ्रातृसमं वचः ॥
data.md: Dhritarashtra said Having attained the generalship of the army and been addressed by the king himself in sweet and brotherly terms and thereupon having ordered the troops to be arranged in battle-array towards the rise of the Sun, relate to me, O Sanjaya, what did the highly intellectual son of Vikartana, Karna, do at that time.

data.v: योगमाज्ञाप्य सेनाया आदित्येऽभ्युदिते तदा । अकरोत्किं महाप्राज्ञस्तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय ॥
कर्णस्य मतमाज्ञाय पुत्रस्ते भरतर्षभ । योगमाज्ञापयामास नान्दीतूर्यपुरःसरम् ॥
data.md: Sanjaya said O foremost of the Bharata race, your sons, having understood the object of Karna, ordered for the arrangement of the troops, followed by a joyful music of various instruments.

data.v: महत्यपररात्रे तु तव पुत्रस्य मारिष । योगो योगेति सहसा प्रादुरासीन्महास्वनः ॥
data.md: Towards the close of the night, O lord of earth, a loud noise arose from amongst your soldiers, saying 'array and array.'

data.v: नागानां कल्पमानानां रथानां च वरूथिनाम् । संनह्यतां पदातीनां वाजिनां च विशां पते ॥
क्रोशतां चापि योधानां त्वरितानां परस्परम् । बभूव तुमुलः शब्दो दिवस्पृक्सुमहांस्तदा ॥
data.md: Thereupon, O lord of the world, there was a terrible uproar of the best of elephants and cars overlaid with beautiful coverlets, whilst they were being equipped and of the infantry crying out in joy, of the horses, whilst being harnessed and of the warriors, whilst moving to and fro, as as shouting to one another in mirth's. The uproar was so very great that it reached the very heavens.

data.v: ततः श्वेतपताकेन बालार्काकारवाजिना । हेमपृष्ठेन धनुषा हस्तिकक्ष्येण केतुना ॥
तूणेन शरपूर्णेन साङ्गदेन वरूथिना । शतघ्नीकिङ्किणीशक्तिशूलतोमरधारिणा ॥
कार्मुकेणोपपन्नेन विमलादित्यवर्चसा । रथेनातिपताकेन सूतपुत्रो व्यदृश्यत ॥
धमन्तं वारिजं तात हेमजालविभूषितम् । विधुन्वानं महच्चापं कार्तस्वरविभूषितम् ॥
data.md: O monarch, (Karna then began) to blow his conch adorned with a net-work of gold and also to shake his terrible bow studded with gold.

data.v: दृष्ट्वा कर्णं महेष्वासं रथस्थं रथिनां वरम् । भानुमन्तमिवोद्यन्तं तमो घ्नन्तं सहस्रशः ॥
data.md: Having seen Karna, that mighty bowman, that foremost of car-warriors, who was seated on his car and also was like the risen Sun destroying the thick darkness and who also was unapproachable.

data.v: न भीष्मव्यसनं केचिन्नापि द्रोणस्य मारिष । नान्येषां पुरुषव्याघ्र मेनिरे तत्र कौरवाः ॥
data.md: None of the Kauravas, O sire, O foremost of persons, considered the fall of eithe, Bhishma, or Drona, or other warriors to be a loss at the time.

data.v: ततस्तु त्वरयन्योधाञ्शङ्खशब्देन मारिष । कर्णो निष्कासयामास कौरवाणां वरूथिनीम् ॥
data.md: Thereupon, O sire Karna, having ordered the warriors to make haste by the sound of his conch, led the vast army of the Kauravas.

data.v: व्यूहं व्यूह्य महेष्वासो माकरं शत्रुतापनः । प्रत्युद्ययौ तदा कर्णः पाण्डवान्विजिगीषया ॥
data.md: Then Karna, that powerful bowman, that siniter of enemies, having arranged the troops in the from of a Makara, started against the Pandavas with the object of winning victory (over them).

data.v: मकरस्य तु तुण्डे वै कर्णो राजन्व्यवस्थितः । नेत्राभ्यां शकुनिः शूर उलूकश्च महारथः ॥
data.md: O king, Karna placed himself in the tip of the beak of that Makara; and the heroic Shakuni and the great car-warrior Uluka were stationed in both the eyes.

data.v: द्रोणपुत्रस्तु शिरसि ग्रीवायां सर्वसोदराः । मध्ये दुर्योधनो राजा बलेन महता वृतः ॥
data.md: The son of Drona was stationed in the head; and all the uterine brothers were in the neck. King Duryodhana was stationed in the middle, surrounded by a large force.

data.v: वामे पादे तु राजेन्द्र कृतवर्मा व्यवस्थितः । नारायणबलैर्युक्तो गोपालैर्युद्धदुर्मदः ॥
data.md: O lord of kings, Kritavarman was placed in the left foot, who was attended by the Narayana-army, namely the Gopalas, most difficult to be vanquished in battle.

data.v: पादे तु दक्षिणे राजन्गौतमः सत्यविक्रमः । त्रिगर्तैश्च महेष्वासैर्दाक्षिणात्यैश्च संवृतः ॥
data.md: O king, the son of Gautama, possessed of the unbaffled prowess, was stationed in right foot, encompassed by the most powerful bowmen, the Trigartas and the troops from the south.

data.md: O great king, Sushena of certain resolution was stationed in the right hind-foot, encompassed by a force of one thousand cars and three hundred elephants.

data.v: समुद्यतकराभ्यां तौ द्विपाभ्यां कृतिनावुभौ । वातोद्धूतपताकाभ्यां युयुधाते महाबलौ ॥
data.md: Again mounting upon their elephants, that had their trunks raised up in the air and that were adorned with banners floating on the wind, both the heroes, perfectly accomplished and possessed of immense strength, went on combating.

data.v: तावन्योन्यस्य धनुषी छित्त्वान्योन्यं विनेदतुः । शक्तितोमरवर्षेण प्रावृण्मेघाविवाम्बुभिः ॥
data.md: Thereupon both of them, having cut-off each other's bow, roared and poured forth showers of arrows and lances upon each other, even as the two masses of clouds during the rainy season drop down rains.

data.v: क्षेमधूर्तिस्तदा भीमं तोमरेण स्तनान्तरे । निर्बिभेद तु वेगेन षड्भिश्चाप्यपरैर्नदन् ॥
data.md: Then having roared aloud Kshemadhurti pierced Bhima in the chest with great force by means of his lance, as well as by six other (lances).

data.v: स भीमसेनः शुशुभे तोमरैरङ्गमाश्रितैः । क्रोधदीप्तवपुर्मेघैः सप्तसप्तिरिवांशुमान् ॥
data.md: That Bhimasena, whose form looked bright with rage, shone with those lances adhering to his body like the resplendent Sun with the masses of clouds about him.

data.v: ततो भास्करवर्णाभमञ्जोगतिमयस्मयम् । ससर्ज तोमरं भीमः प्रत्यमित्राय यत्नवान् ॥
data.md: Thereupon, Bhima thrust at his enemy most carefully the lance, made of iron, that had the splendour of the colour of the solar rays and had a speed, direct and straight.

data.v: ततः कुलूताधिपतिश्चापमायम्य सायकैः । दशभिस्तोमरं छित्त्वा शक्त्या विव्याध पाण्डवम् ॥
data.md: Thereupon having stretched out his bow, the lord of the Kulatas severed the lance by means of ten arrows and pierced the son of Pandu (Bhima) by sixty other shafts.

data.v: अथ कार्मुकमादाय महाजलदनिस्वनम् । रिपोरभ्यर्दयन्नागमुन्मदः पाण्डवः शरैः ॥
data.md: Then having taken up his bow having the twang like the roar of clouds, Bhima the son of Pandu, oppressed his enemy's elephant by arrows and uttered terrible shouts.

data.v: स शरौघार्दितो नागो भीमसेनेन संयुगे । निगृह्यमाणो नातिष्ठद्वातध्वस्त इवाम्बुदः ॥
data.md: That elephant, being thus oppressed by the arrows of Bhimasena, did not stay in the field of battle, although repeatedly restrained, even as the cloud dispersed by the wind (run away from their positions).

data.v: तामभ्यधावद्द्विरदं भीमसेनस्य नागराट् । महावातेरितं मेघं वातोद्धूत इवाम्बुदः ॥
data.md: The most formidable and royal elephant of Bhima rapidly followed that elephant of (Kshemadhurti), even as the wind-blown cloud pursues the cloud dispersed by the tempest.

data.v: संनिवर्त्यात्मनो नागं क्षेमधूर्तिः प्रयत्नतः । विव्याधाभिद्रुतं बाणैर्भीमसेनं सकुञ्जरम् ॥
data.md: Kshemadhurti of immense energy having checked his own elephant, pierced with his arrows the elephant of Bhimasena pursuing his own.

data.v: ततः साधुविसृष्टेन क्षुरेण पुरुषर्षभः । छित्त्वा शरासनं शत्रोर्नागमामित्रमार्दयत् ॥
data.md: Thereupon, he (Kshemadhurti), having cutoff his enemy's bow by means of an arrow well-shot, razor-like and straight, highly oppressed that elephant belonging to his foe.

data.v: ततः खजाकया भीमं क्षेमधूर्तिः पराभिनत् । जघान चास्य द्विरदं नाराचैः सर्वमर्मसु ॥
data.md: Then highly wrathful Kshemadhurti struck Bhima in the battle and killed the elephant by piercing all his vital parts with his arrows.

data.v: पुरा नागस्य पतनादवप्लुत्य स्थितो महीम् । भीमसेनो रिपोर्नागं गदया समपोथयत् ॥
तस्मात्प्रमथितान्नागात्क्षेमधूर्तिमवद्रुतम् । उद्यतासिमुपायान्तं गदयाहन्वृकोदरः ॥
data.md: Then he, too, struck down the elephant of his enemy by means of his mace. Then Vrikodara killed Kshemadhurti with his mace, who then had descended from his crushed elephant and had advanced against him with uplifted weapons. Having been thus killed, he, with a sword in the hand, fell down dead by the side of his elephant.

data.v: स पपात हतः सासिर्व्यसुः स्वमभितो द्विपम् । वज्रप्ररुग्णमचलं सिंहो वज्रहतो यथा ॥
निहतं नृपतिं दृष्ट्वा कुलूतानां यशस्करम् । प्राद्रवद्व्यथिता सेना त्वदीया भरतर्षभ ॥
data.md: O foremost of the Bharata race, even as a lion killed by thunder falls dead by the side of a hill broken down by thunder. having seen the most famous lord of the Kulatas killed, your troops, highly distressed, ran away from ihe field.

data.v: ततः कर्णो महेष्वासः पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम् । जघान समरे शूरः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः ॥
data.md: Sanjaya said Then the mighty bowman, the heroic Karna, killed the troops of the Pandavas in battle with the straight arrows.

data.v: तथैव पाण्डवा राजंस्तव पुत्रस्य वाहिनीम् । कर्णस्य प्रमुखे क्रुद्धा विनिजघ्नुर्महारथाः ॥
data.md: O king, the mighty car-warriors, namely the Pandavas, had most wrathfully smitten the soldiers of your son in the same way in the very presence of Karna.

data.v: कर्णो राजन्महाबाहुर्न्यवधीत्पाण्डवीं चमूम् । नाराचैरर्करश्म्याभैः कर्मारपरिमार्जितैः ॥
data.md: So also Karna, O monarch, began to smite the army belonging to the Pandavas in the field of battle with the arrows, that were bright like the rays of the sun and excellently polished by the black-smith.

data.v: तत्र भारत कर्णेन नाराचैस्ताडिता गजाः । नेदुः सेदुश्च मम्लुश्च बभ्रमुश्च दिशो दश ॥
data.md: O descendant of the Bharata race, there (in the field of battle) the elephants highly afflicted by Karna with his straight arrows, roared most loudly, became weakened and senseless and ran away towards the ten points of the horizon.

data.v: वध्यमाने बले तस्मिन्सूतपुत्रेण मारिष । नकुलोऽभ्यद्रवत्तूर्णं सूतपुत्रं महारणे ॥
data.md: O father, while that immense force was being killed by the son of Suta, Nakula proceeded against that mighty car-warrior, the son of the Suta with great rapidity.

data.v: भीमसेनस्तथा द्रौणिं कुर्वाणं कर्म दुष्करम् । विन्दानुविन्दौ कैकेयौ सात्यकिः समवारयत् ॥
data.md: Then Bhimasena checked the progress of Drona's son, who was achieving the most arduous tasks and Satyaki, that of the two Kaikeya princes, Vindu and Anuvindu.

data.v: श्रुतकर्माणमायान्तं चित्रसेनो महीपतिः । प्रतिविन्ध्यं तथा चित्रश्चित्रकेतनकार्मुकः ॥
data.md: The lord of the earth, Chitrasena, rushed towards Srutakarman, who was advancing against him; so also Prativindhya towards Chitra, who carried a standard of diverse colours and a beautiful bow.

data.v: दुर्योधनस्तु राजानं धर्मपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम् । संशप्तकगणान्क्रुद्धो अभ्यधावद्धनंजयः ॥
data.md: Duryodhana, too, proceeded against the king Yudhishthira the son of Dhrama, while Dhananjaya rushed against the wrathful Samsaptakas.

data.v: धृष्टद्युम्नः कृपं चाथ तस्मिन्वीरवरक्षये । शिखण्डी कृतवर्माणं समासादयदच्युतम् ॥
data.md: While that whole host of the foretnost heroes was being thus slain, Dhrishtadyumna rushed against Kripa; and that undecayable Shikhandin proceeded against Kritavarman.

data.v: श्रुतकीर्तिस्तथा शल्यं माद्रीपुत्रः सुतं तव । दुःशासनं महाराज सहदेवः प्रतापवान् ॥
data.md: O mighty monarch, so again, Shrutakirti closed with Shalya; and that son of Madri, Shahadeva of immense prowess, closed with your son, Dussashana.

data.v: केकयौ सात्यकिं युद्धे शरवर्षेण भास्वता । सात्यकिः केकयौ चैव छादयामास भारत ॥
data.md: In that great battle, the two Kaikeya princes covered Satyaki with a shower of arrows. Satyaki on the other hand covered the two Kaikeya princes (with a shower of brilliant arrows, O descendant of the Bharata race).

data.v: तावेनं भ्रातरौ वीरं जघ्नतुर्हृदये भृशम् । विषाणाभ्यां यथा नागौ प्रतिनागं महाहवे ॥
data.md: Those two heroic brothers deeply pierced this warrior (Satyaki) in the chest, even as two elephant strike another hostile elephant with their tusks in a dense forest.

data.v: शरसंभिन्नवर्माणौ तावुभौ भ्रातरौ रणे । सात्यकिं सत्यकर्माणं राजन्विव्यधतुः शरैः ॥
data.md: O monarch, these two heroic brothers whose vital parts were deeply struck with the arrows, pierced Satyaki, who always performed appropriate deeds with their shafts,

data.v: तौ सात्यकिर्महाराज प्रहसन्सर्वतोदिशम् । छादयञ्शरवर्षेण वारयामास भारत ॥
data.md: O powerful monarch, Satyaki on the other hand, having smiled and shrouded all the points of the horizon with a shower of arrows, closed with the two brothers, O descendant of the Bharata race.

data.v: वार्यमाणौ ततस्तौ तु शैनेयशरवृष्टिभिः । शैनेयस्य रथं तूर्णं छादयामासतुः शरैः ॥
data.md: Thereupon those two brothers, whose progress was checked by the shower of arrows of Sini's grandson, indeed, covered the car of Sini's grandson with lots of shafts.

data.v: तयोस्तु धनुषी चित्रे छित्त्वा शौरिर्महाहवे । अथ तौ सायकैस्तीक्ष्णैश्छादयामास दुःसहैः ॥
data.md: Having severed the most beautiful bows of those two brothers, then the highly celebrated Shauri restrained the progress of them both in the battle with a shower of sharp arrows.

data.v: अथान्ये धनुषी मृष्टे प्रगृह्य च महाशरान् । सात्यकिं पूरयन्तौ तौ चेरतुर्लघु सुष्ठु च ॥
data.md: Then having grasped two other beautiful bows and most effective shafts, they two, too, shrounded Satyaki (with the arrows) and roved about in the field with immense activity and expertness.

data.v: ताभ्यां मुक्ता महाबाणाः कङ्कबर्हिणवाससः । द्योतयन्तो दिशः सर्वाः संपेतुः स्वर्णभूषणाः ॥
data.md: Those mighty arrows, shot by the two brothers, adorned with the feathers of the Kanka and the peacock and ornamented with gold, fell down (upon the foes), after having illumined all the points of the horizon.

data.v: बाणान्धकारमभवत्तयो राजन्महाहवे । अन्योन्यस्य धनुश्चैव चिच्छिदुस्ते महारथाः ॥
data.md: O monarch, there was a gloom in that formidable battle owing to the shower of arrows shot by both the parties. Then those great car-warriors severed each other's bows.

data.v: ततः क्रुद्धो महाराज सात्वतो युद्धदुर्मदः । धनुरन्यत्समादाय सज्यं कृत्वा च संयुगे । क्षुरप्रेण सुतीक्ष्णेन अनुविन्दशिरोऽहरत् ॥
data.md: Thereupon, O mighty monarch, wrathful Satvata, most invincible in the field, having taken up another bow and stretched its string properly, severed the head of Anuvinda with an arrow, sharp like the razor.

data.v: तच्छिरो न्यपतद्भूमौ कुण्डलोत्पीडितं महत् । शम्बरस्य शिरो यद्वन्निहतस्य महारणे । शोषयन्केकयान्सर्वाञ्जगामाशु वसुंधराम् ॥
data.md: O monarch, that mighty head, adorned with ear-rings, fell like the head of Shambara, slain in that dreadful battle (of old). This, having fallen upon the earth most rapidly, greatly aggrieved all the Kaikayas.

data.v: तं दृष्ट्वा निहतं शूरं भ्राता तस्य महारथः । सज्यमन्यद्धनुः कृत्वा शैनेयं प्रत्यवारयत् ॥
data.md: Having seen that hero slain, his brother, that mighty car-warrior (Vinda), after having stretched out the string of another bow, restrained the course of Shini's grandson.

data.v: स शक्त्या सात्यकिं विद्ध्वा स्वर्णपुङ्खैः शिलाशितैः । ननाद बलवन्नादं तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत् ॥
data.md: Having pierced Satyaki with sixty shafts, all sharpened on stone and adorned with the feathers of gold, he roared most loudly and said-wait, wait.

data.v: स सात्यकिं पुनः क्रुद्धः केकयानां महारथः । शरैरग्निशिखाकारैर्बाह्वोरुरसि चार्दयत् ॥
data.md: The mighty car-warrior of the Kaikeya troops then pierced Satyaki in his arms and chest most rapidly with several thousands of arrows.

data.v: स शरैः क्षतसर्वाङ्गः सात्वतः सत्त्वकोविदः । रराज समरे राजन्सपत्र इव किंशुकः ॥
data.md: O king, Satyaki, of true prowess, being thus wounded with the arrows in all his limbs, shone in the field of battle like a Kinshuka with flowers.

data.v: सात्यकिः समरे विद्धः केकयेन महात्मना । केकयं पञ्चविंशत्या विव्याध प्रहसन्निव ॥
data.md: In the battle, Satyaki, having been pierced by the lofty-minded Kaikeya, smilingly pierced back the Kaikeya chief with twenty-five shafts.

data.v: शतचन्द्रचिते गृह्य चर्मणी सुभुजौ तु तौ । व्यरोचेतां महारङ्गे निस्त्रिंशवरधारिणौ । यथा देवासुरे युद्धे जम्भशक्रौ महाबलौ ॥
मण्डलानि ततस्तौ च विचरन्तौ महारणे । अन्योन्यमसिभिस्तूर्णं समाजघ्नतुराहवे ॥
केकयस्य ततश्चर्म द्विधा चिच्छेद सात्वतः । सात्यकेश्च तथैवासौ चर्म चिच्छेद पार्थिवः ॥
data.md: Thus the two, again, made the best of their efforts in slaying each other. Then Satvata severed the shield of the Kaikeya chief into two pieces. So also this Vinda severed the shield of Satyaki into two pieces.

data.v: चर्म च्छित्त्वा तु कैकेयस्तारागणशतैर्वृतम् । चचार मण्डलान्येव गतप्रत्यागतानि च ॥
data.md: The Kaikeya chief, indeed, having thus broken into pieces the shield, that was decked with hundred of stars, roved in circles in the field, sometimes advancing and sometimes receding back.

data.v: तं चरन्तं महारङ्गे निस्त्रिंशवरधारिणम् । अपहस्तेन चिच्छेद शैनेयस्त्वरयान्वितः ॥
data.md: Thereupon the grandson of Shini who was possessed with greatest activity severed him (his head) who having grasped the best of swords, careered in the broad field of battle, by a side-stroke.

data.v: सवर्मा केकयो राजन्द्विधा छिन्नो महाहवे । निपपात महेष्वासो वज्रनुन्न इवाचलः ॥
data.md: O monarch, the Kaikeya prince, that mighty bowman, who was adorned with the shield, being thus cut-off into pieces in that dreadful battle, fell down like a hill broken down by a thunderbolt.

data.v: तं निहत्य रणे शूरः शैनेयो रथसत्तमः । युधामन्यो रथं तूर्णमारुरोह परंतपः ॥
data.md: That war-like grandson of Shini, that best of car-warriors, that scorcher of enemies, after having slain him (the Kaikeya chief) in battle, immediately ascended the car of Yudhamanyu.

data.v: ततोऽन्यं रथमास्थाय विधिवत्कल्पितं पुनः । केकयानां महत्सैन्यं व्यधमत्सात्यकिः शरैः ॥
data.md: Thereupon, again, having ascended another car, that furnished with its its due equipment's, Satyaki began to destroy the immense army of the Kaikeyas with his was arrows.

data.v: सा वध्यमाना समरे केकयस्य महाचमूः । तमुत्सृज्य रथं शत्रुं प्रदुद्राव दिशो दश ॥
data.md: That vast force of the Kaikeyas, being slaughtered in battle, left that enemy in the field and ran away in the ten different directions of the horizon.

data.v: श्रुतकर्मा महाराज चित्रसेनं महीपतिम् । आजघ्ने समरे क्रुद्धः पञ्चाशद्भिः शिलीमुखैः ॥
data.md: Sanjaya said Thereupon, O monarch, the wrathful Shrutakarman had slain down Chitrasena, the lord of the earth, in the battle, by means of fifty different arrows.

data.v: अभिसारस्तु तं राजा नवभिर्निशितैः शरैः । श्रुतकर्माणमाहत्य सूतं विव्याध पञ्चभिः ॥
data.md: O king, Avishara, indeed, after having struck down that Shrutakarman with nine straight shafts, pierced his driver with five other arrows.

data.v: श्रुतकर्मा ततः क्रुद्धश्चित्रसेनं चमूमुखे । नाराचेन सुतीक्ष्णेन मर्मदेशे समर्दयत् ॥
data.md: Wrathful Shrutakarman, on the other hand, had struck down that Chitrasena, who was then standing at the head of his force, with a keen arrow in the most vital part of his body.

data.v: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे चैनं श्रुतकीर्तिर्महायशाः । नवत्या जगतीपालं छादयामास पत्रिभिः ॥
data.md: During this interval, the highly famous Shrutakirtin closed this ruler of the earth (his insensible foe) with ninety different shafts.

data.v: प्रतिलभ्य ततः संज्ञां चित्रसेनो महारथः । धनुश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन तं च विव्याध सप्तभिः ॥
data.md: Thereupon Chitrasena, that mighty bowman, having attained consciousness again, struck down his enemy's bow by a broodheaded shafts and also pierced him with seven arrows.

data.v: सोऽन्यत्कार्मुकमादाय वेगघ्नं रुक्मभूषणम् । चित्ररूपतरं चक्रे चित्रसेनं शरोर्मिभिः ॥
data.md: Then he (Shrutakarman) took up another bow, that was capable of casting away fierce arrows and was adorned with gold, made Chitrasena, by piercing him with the torrents of shafts, wear a varied appearance. to

data.v: स शरैश्चित्रितो राजंश्चित्रमाल्यधरो युवा । युवेव समशोभत्स गोष्ठीमध्ये स्वलंकृतः ॥
data.md: That youthful prince, wearing an wonderful appearance with the shafts and putting on handsome garlands, shone in the field of battle, like an youth, excellently decked with ornaments, in the midst of an assembly.

data.v: श्रुतकर्माणमथ वै नाराचेन स्तनान्तरे । बिभेद समरे क्रुद्धस्तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत् ॥
data.md: O monarch, he, indeed, then pierced Shrutakarman in the chest with a keen shaft immediately; and afterwards uttered him-'wait and wait.'

data.v: श्रुतकर्मापि समरे नाराचेन समर्दितः । सुस्राव रुधिरं भूरि गैरिकाम्भ इवाचलः ॥
data.md: There Shrutakarman, on the other hand, being thus pierced by the arrow in the field of battle, began to shed blood, even as a mountain lets the liquid red chalk flow down.

data.v: ततः स रुधिराक्ताङ्गो रुधिरेण कृतच्छविः । रराज समरे राजन्सपुष्प इव किंशुकः ॥
data.md: O king, Satyaki, of true prowess, being thus wounded with the arrows in all his limbs, shone in the field of battle like a Kinshuka with flowers.

data.v: श्रुतकर्मा ततो राजञ्शत्रूणां समभिद्रुतः । शत्रुसंवरणं कृत्वा द्विधा चिच्छेद कार्मुकम् ॥
data.md: At that time, O monarch, Shrutakarman, having been attacked by his antagonist (Chitrasena), became very wrathful and severed his bow, that was capable of resisting the enemies, into two pieces.

data.v: अथैनं छिन्नधन्वानं नाराचानां त्रिभिः शतैः । विव्याध भरतश्रेष्ठ श्रुतकर्मा महायशाः ॥
ततोऽपरेण भल्लेन भृशं तीक्ष्णेन सत्वरः । जहार सशिरस्त्राणं शिरस्तस्य महात्मनः ॥
data.md: Thereupon he had severed the head of that high-souled one, that was adorned with an (iron) protection, with another broad-headed, pointed and sharp-headed arrow.

data.v: तच्छिरो न्यपतद्भूमौ सुमहच्चित्रवर्मणः । यदृच्छया यथा चन्द्रश्च्युतः स्वर्गान्महीतले ॥
data.md: That head of Chitrasena, which looked most resplendent, fell down upon the earth, even as the moon, out of her own will, falls upon the ground, being loosened from heaven.

data.v: राजानं निहतं दृष्ट्वा अभिसारं च मारिष । अभ्यद्रवन्त वेगेन चित्रसेनस्य सैनिकाः ॥
data.md: O sire, the troops of Chitrasena, having seen their king slain, marched with great rapidity against Avishara.

data.v: ततः क्रुद्धो महेष्वासस्तत्सैन्यं प्राद्रवच्छरैः । अन्तकाले यथा क्रुद्धः सर्वभूतानि प्रेतराट् । द्रावयन्निषुभिस्तूर्णं श्रुतकर्मा व्यरोचत ॥
data.md: Thereupon that mighty bowman, who became very wrathful, rushed against those troops, shooting arrows upon them; even as, during the period of universal dissolution the king of the nether world (Yama), filled with wrath, rushes against all creatures.

data.v: प्रतिविन्ध्यस्ततश्चित्रं भित्त्वा पञ्चभिराशुगैः । सारथिं त्रिभिरानर्च्छद्ध्वजमेकेषुणा ततः ॥
data.md: Thereupon Prativindhya pierced Chitra with five rapid-going shafts and pierced the driver of his car with three others. Then he broke down his standard by a single arrow. as

data.v: तं चित्रो नवभिर्भल्लैर्बाह्वोरुरसि चार्दयत् । स्वर्णपुङ्खैः शिलाधौतैः कङ्कबर्हिणवाजितैः ॥
data.md: Then he, (Chitra) pierced him by throwing at his arms and chest nine broad-handed shafts, that were adorned with the wings of gold and sharp points and ornamented with the feathers of the Kanka and peacock.

data.v: प्रतिविन्ध्यो धनुस्तस्य छित्त्वा भारत सायकैः । पञ्चभिर्निशितैर्बाणैरथैनं संप्रजघ्निवान् ॥
data.md: O descendant of the Bharata race, Prativindhya, having severed his (enemy's) bow with keen arrows, slaughtered him with five well-sharpened shafts.

data.v: ततः शक्तिं महाराज हेमदण्डां दुरासदाम् । प्राहिणोत्तव पुत्राय घोरामग्निशिखामिव ॥
data.md: Thereupon, O great king, he (Chitra) threw at your grandson the shaft, called Shakti, which was decked with golden bells and which, again, was most irresistible and dreadful and which also, was like the flame of fire.

data.v: तामापतन्तीं सहसा शक्तिमुल्कामिवाम्बरात् । द्विधा चिच्छेद समरे प्रतिविन्ध्यो हसन्निव ॥
data.md: Prativindhya, as if laughing, severed into two pieces that shaft, in the field of battle, falling upon him, which was like a great flashing meteor suddenly falling from the sky.

data.v: सा पपात तदा छिन्ना प्रतिविन्ध्यशरैः शितैः । युगान्ते सर्वभूतानि त्रासयन्ती यथाशनिः ॥
data.md: That shaft which was cut-off into three pieces by the keen arrows of Prativindhya, fell down like the thunderbolt, during the period of expiration of the Yuga, thus inspiring great fear in all creatures.

data.v: शक्तिं तां प्रहतां दृष्ट्वा चित्रो गृह्य महागदाम् । प्रतिविन्ध्याय चिक्षेप रुक्मजालविभूषिताम् ॥
data.md: Having seen that arrows, called Shakti, severed into pieces, Chitra took up his powerful mace, that was adorned with a network of gold and threw it against Prativindhya.

data.v: सा जघान हयांस्तस्य सारथिं च महारणे । रथं प्रमृद्य वेगेन धरणीमन्वपद्यत ॥
data.md: That mace had smitten his (antagonist's) heroes and the driver of his car in that great battle and then, having smitten his car, fell impetuously upon the ground.

data.v: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु रथादाप्लुत्य भारत । शक्तिं चिक्षेप चित्राय स्वर्णघण्टामलंकृताम् ॥
data.md: O descendant of the Bharata race, he (Prativindhya), in the mean time, having descended from his car, threw at Chitra the arrow, called Shakti, that was furnished with golden balls and decked with several ornaments.

data.v: तामापतन्तीं जग्राह चित्रो राजन्महामनाः । ततस्तामेव चिक्षेप प्रतिविन्ध्याय भारत ॥
data.md: The high-minded king Chitra caught hold of it (that shaft), whilst it was falling upon him; and thereafter, O descendant of Bharata race, he threw it back at Prativindhya.

data.v: समासाद्य रणे शूरं प्रतिविन्ध्यं महाप्रभा । निर्भिद्य दक्षिणं बाहुं निपपात महीतले । पतिताभासयच्चैव तं देशमशनिर्यथा ॥
data.md: That highly resplendent shaft, having pierced heroic Prativindhya in the field of battle and also having penetrated through his right arm, fell down upon the ground; and as it fell, it illuminated that whole region (the battlefield) by its splendour, even as the lightning, falling upon the carth, illumines the entire place, where it falls.

data.v: प्रतिविन्ध्यस्ततो राजंस्तोमरं हेमभूषितम् । प्रेषयामास संक्रुद्धश्चित्रस्य वधकाम्यया ॥
data.md: Thereupon, O monarch, the most wrathful Prativindhya, most desirous of slaying Chitra, hurled at him a lance adorned with gold.

data.v: स तस्य देवावरणं भित्त्वा हृदयमेव च । जगाम धरणीं तूर्णं महोरग इवाशयम् ॥
data.md: That lance, having pierced through his armour and chest, immediately fell down upon the earth; even as the gigantic serpent enters into its hole.

data.v: स पपात तदा राजंस्तोमरेण समाहतः । प्रसार्य विपुलौ बाहू पीनौ परिघसंनिभौ ॥
data.md: Then that king, having been smitten by the lance, fell upon the earth, stretching out his two long and massive arms, that resembled two iron clubs in splendour.

data.v: चित्रं संप्रेक्ष्य निहतं तावका रणशोभिनः । अभ्यद्रवन्त वेगेन प्रतिविन्ध्यं समन्ततः ॥
data.md: Having seen Chitra slain (in the battle), the troops on your side, who are all ornaments of battle, rushed from all sides with great impetuosity against Pritivindhya.

data.v: सृजन्तो विविधान्बाणाञ्शतघ्नीश्च सकिङ्किणीः । त एनं छादयामासुः सूर्यमभ्रगणा इव ॥
data.md: Shooting several kinds of arms and the shaft called Shataghni, that was ornamented with the rows of bells (those troops) covered him all ever, even as the clouds cover the Sun.

data.v: तानपास्य महाबाहुः शरजालेन संयुगे । व्यद्रावयत्तव चमूं वज्रहस्त इवासुरीम् ॥
data.md: That mighty-armed one (Prativindhya), having struck those warriors with a net-work of arrows in the field of battle, over threw your force, Indra, who carried the thunderbolt in the hand, over-threw the Asura host.

data.v: ते वध्यमानाः समरे तावकाः पाण्डवैर्नृप । विप्रकीर्यन्त सहसा वातनुन्ना घना इव ॥
data.md: Thus slain in the battle by the Pandavas, the troops on your side, O monarch, suddenly broke in all directions, even as the clouds, scattered by the wind, run away in all sides.

data.v: विप्रद्रुते बले तस्मिन्वध्यमाने समन्ततः । द्रौणिरेकोऽभ्ययात्तूर्णं भीमसेनं महाबलम् ॥
data.md: Amongst your whole force, that was immensely slain and (the rest) running away from the field, the son of Drona alone proceeded with great impetuosity against that highly powerful Bhimasena.

data.v: ततः समागमो घोरो बभूव सहसा तयोः । यथा देवासुरे युद्धे वृत्रवासवयोरभूत् ॥
data.md: Then there suddenly followed a dreadful conflict between these two parties; even as there took place an encounter between Vritra even and Vashava (Indra) in the battle between the celestials and the Asuras. and Vashava (Indra) in the battle between the celestials and the Asuras.

data.v: भीमसेनं ततो द्रौणी राजन्विव्याध पत्रिणा । त्वरया परया युक्तो दर्शयन्नस्त्रलाघवम् ॥
data.md: Sanjaya said Thereupon, O king, the son of Drona, who was possessed of great alacrity and who showed easiness in the management of weapons, pierced Bhimasena with an arrow.

data.v: अथैनं पुनराजघ्ने नवत्या निशितैः शरैः । सर्वमर्माणि संप्रेक्ष्य मर्मज्ञो लघुहस्तवत् ॥
data.md: In the same way, he (the son of Drona), who was well acquainted with the different vital parts of the body and who, again, was very smart in the management of his arms, after having seen all the vital parts of his body, had struck him with ninety sharp-headed shafts.

data.v: भीमसेनः समाकीर्णो द्रौणिना निशितैः शरैः । रराज समरे राजन्रश्मिवानिव भास्करः ॥
data.md: O monarch. Bhimasenc, having been closed with a shower of keen arrows by the son of Drona, shone in the field of battle like the sun with all his rays.

data.v: ततः शरसहस्रेण सुप्रयुक्तेन पाण्डवः । द्रोणपुत्रमवच्छाद्य सिंहनादममुञ्चत ॥
data.md: Thereupon the Pandava, after having covered the son of Drona with one thousand arrows, well-aimed, sent forth a leonine roar.

data.v: शरैः शरांस्ततो द्रौणिः संवार्य युधि पाण्डवम् । ललाटेऽभ्यहनद्राजन्नाराचेन स्मयन्निव ॥
data.md: Then, O monarch, the son of Drona, having checked the course of his (antagonist's) shafts by his own arrows in the field of battle, smilingly struck the son of Pandu in the forehead with a dart.

data.v: ललाटस्थं ततो बाणं धारयामास पाण्डवः । यथा शृङ्गं वने दृप्तः खड्गो धारयते नृप ॥
data.md: Thereafter, O king, the son of (Pandu), carried the shafts, that was struck in his forehead; even as the proud rhinoceros in the forest bears his horn.

data.v: ततो द्रौणिं रणे भीमो यतमानं पराक्रमी । त्रिभिर्विव्याध नाराचैर्ललाटे विस्मयन्निव ॥
data.md: Then Bhima of immense prowess smilingly pierced the son of Drona, who attempted very hard in the battle, in the forehead with three shafts.

data.v: ललाटस्थैस्ततो बाणैर्ब्राह्मणः स व्यरोचत । प्रावृषीव यथा सिक्तस्त्रिशृङ्गः पर्वतोत्तमः ॥
data.md: Then this twice-born person looked most resplendent with the arrows struck in his forehead; even as the best of mountains, being washed (with water) during the rainy season, looks resplendent with its three peaks.

data.v: ततः शरशतैर्द्रौणिमर्दयामास पाण्डवः । न चैनं कम्पयामास मातरिश्वेव पर्वतम् ॥
data.md: Thus the son of Drona afflicted the son of Pandu with hundreds of arrows, but he could not shake him; even as the wind cannot shake the mountain.

data.v: तथैव पाण्डवं युद्धे द्रौणिः शरशतैः शितैः । नाकम्पयत संहृष्टो वार्योघ इव पर्वतम् ॥
data.md: In the same way, the son of Pandu, highly gratified, could not shake the son of Drona, in the field of battle, with hundreds of his sharphanded arrows; even as the torrents of rain cannot shake the mountain.

data.v: तावन्योन्यं शरैर्घोरैश्छादयानौ महारथौ । रथचर्यागतौ शूरौ शुशुभाते रणोत्कटौ ॥
data.md: Those two mighty car-warriors, the two heroic warriors of terrible prowess, having covered each other with their dreadful shafts, looked very handsome, sitting upon their cars.

data.v: आदित्याविव संदीप्तौ लोकक्षयकरावुभौ । स्वरश्मिभिरिवान्योन्यं तापयन्तौ शरोत्तमैः ॥
data.md: Both (the heroes) looked resplendent like two suns and were destructive of men on each other's side. Moreover both of them burnt each other by their own excellent arrows, that resembled their own rays.

data.v: कृतप्रतिकृते यत्नं कुर्वाणौ च महारणे । कृतप्रतिकृते यत्नं चक्राते तावभीतवत् ॥
व्याघ्राविव च संग्रामे चेरतुस्तौ महारथौ । शरदंष्ट्रौ दुराधर्षौ चापव्यात्तौ भयानकौ ॥
data.md: Those two foremost of persons, those invincible and fierce heroes, whose teeth were constituted by the shafts and whose mouths were formed by the bows, roved about in the field of battle like two terrible tigers.

data.v: अभूतां तावदृश्यौ च शरजालैः समन्ततः । मेघजालैरिव च्छन्नौ गगने चन्द्रभास्करौ ॥
data.md: Both of them became invisible on account of the torrents of shafts in all sides; even as both the sun and the moon in the firmament become invisible, when they are covered over by the net-work of clouds.

data.v: प्रकाशौ च मुहूर्तेन तत्रैवास्तामरिंदमौ । विमुक्तौ मेघजालेन शशिसूर्यौ यथा दिवि ॥
data.md: Then the two smiters of foes appeared for a very short while and shone forth like Mars and Mercury, when they become wholly released from the cover of clouds.

data.v: अपसव्यं ततश्चक्रे द्रौणिस्तत्र वृकोदरम् । किरञ्शरशतैरुग्रैर्धाराभिरिव पर्वतम् ॥
न तु तन्ममृषे भीमः शत्रोर्विजयलक्षणम् । प्रतिचक्रे च तं राजन्पाण्डवोऽप्यपसव्यतः ॥
मण्डलानां विभागेषु गतप्रत्यागतेषु च । बभूव तुमुलं युद्धं तयोस्तत्र महामृधे ॥
चरित्वा विविधान्मार्गान्मण्डलं स्थानमेव च । शरैः पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैरन्योन्यमभिजघ्नतुः ॥
अन्योन्यस्य वधे यत्नं चक्रतुस्तौ महारथौ । ईषतुर्विरथं चैव कर्तुमन्योन्यमाहवे ॥
ततो द्रौणिर्महास्त्राणि प्रादुश्चक्रे महारथः । तान्यस्त्रैरेव समरे प्रतिजघ्नेऽस्य पाण्डवः ॥
data.md: Again, each of them wished to make the other carless in the field. Thereupon the son of Drona, that mighty car-warrior, imparted strength to the most powerful weapons, which, indeed the son of Pandu frustrated by the weapons of his own, in the battle.

data.v: ततो घोरं महाराज अस्त्रयुद्धमवर्तत । ग्रहयुद्धं यथा घोरं प्रजासंहरणे अभूत् ॥
data.md: Then, O mighty king, there ensued a very dreadful battle of weapons, even as there had taken place a very terrible battle of the planets, during the time of destruction of creatures of the universe.

data.v: ते बाणाः समसज्जन्त क्षिप्तास्ताभ्यां तु भारत । द्योतयन्तो दिशः सर्वास्तच्च सैन्यं समन्ततः ॥
data.md: O descendant of the Bharata race, those arrows, shot by both of them, struck one another, and thus illumined all the points of the i horizon, as well as the troops on your side, from all directions. even

data.v: बाणसंघावृतं घोरमाकाशं समपद्यत । उक्लापातकृतं यद्वत्प्रजानां संक्षये नृप ॥
data.md: O king, the firmament looked very fearful as it was wholly covered by the showers of arrows, it appears during the destruction of the creatures of the universe, when it is entirely shrouded by the fall of the meteors.

data.v: बाणाभिघातात्संजज्ञे तत्र भारत पावकः । सविस्फुलिङ्गो दीप्तार्चिः सोऽदहद्वाहिनीद्वयम् ॥
data.md: O descendant of the Bharata race, there (in the field of battle) was produced a great fire by the counteraction of shafts from both the parties, which, viz. the fire was attended with sparks and blazing flames. It continued to burn both the hosts.

data.md: Then these persons, who having posted there in any way they liked, witnessed the battle, considered themselves to be wholly covered over with the showers of arrows, as if closing themselves by themselves.

data.md: Those arrows of innumerable forms furnished with the wings, having been shot from the Gandiva bow, had slaughtered the elephants, horses and men, either stationed there or at the distance of two miles, in that (dreadful) battle.

data.md: After a short while, the elephants that resembled hill, along with those riding upon them, tumbled down upon the ground even as the large mountains broken down by the thunder-bolt fall upon the ground.

data.md: Dhananjaya, like the sun appearing at the end of the Yuga, had soaked away the vast deep of the Samsaptaka army, that was most difficult to be dried up, by means of his sharpheaded arrows, that constituted his rays.

data.md: Then again he (Dhananjaya) without hesitation perfectly penetrated the son of Drona, who was like a huge mountain with straight arrows, that had great force and also that were as resplendent as the sun; even as the wielder of the thunder-bolt pierces a mountain (by thunder).

data.v: तमाचार्यसुतः क्रुद्धः साश्वयन्तारमाशुगैः । युयुत्सुर्नाशकद्योद्धुं पार्थस्तानन्तराच्छिनत् ॥
data.md: The most wrathful son of the Preceptor, desiring to fight, proceeded against him (Arjuna) with a view to pierce hiin along with his horses and drivers with swift arrows. The son of Pritha, on the other hand, sundered those arrows shot at him.

data.v: ततः परमसंक्रुद्धः काण्डकोशानवासृजत् । अश्वत्थामाभिरूपाय गृहानतिथये यथा ॥
data.md: Thereupon he (the son of Pandu), having been highly wrathful, continued to shower forth quivers of the arrows upon the person of Ashvatihaman; even as one serves a guest with things upon things in his house.

data.md: Then the son of Pandu, after having forsaken the army of the Samsaptakas ran towards the son of Drona; even as the doner, after having abandoned the unworthy quests, rushes towards the worthy one with his gifts.

data.md: Sanjaya said Thereupon the battle waged between them (Arjuna and Ashvatthaman) who were like the planets Sakra and Angirasa in splendour; even as there had taken place a battle between Sakra and Angirasa in the firmament for entering the constellation.

data.md: Those two warriors, who inspired the people of the world with fears, afflicted cach other with resplendent arrows, that were like their rays and resembled two planets, that had gone away from their proper paths.

data.md: Thereupon Arjuna deeply penetrated him (Ashvatthaman) in the midst of his eye-brows with a sharp arrow. Therewith the son of Drona blazed forth like the sun with his upward rays.

data.md: Thus the two Krishnas (Arjuna and Keshava) having been greatly afflicted by Ashvatthaman with hundreds of keen arrows, stood (in the field), blazing forth, covered ever as they were by their own rays, like the two suns appearing at the end of the Yuga.

data.md: That one of immense strength, always performing the most difficult deeds, pierced both Keshava and Arjuna in the most vital part of their bodies with arrows, that were endued with fierce impetuosity. Even death, being struck by them, feels great pain.

data.md: After having restrained the arrows shot by the son of Drona, Arjuna shrouded him over with twice as many shafts, furnished with the wings. He then, having closed over that best hero, the unique of his class, along with his horses, the driver of his car and his standards, began to smite down the army of the Samsaptakas.

data.md: The excellently ornamented cars, horses and elephants, that were ridden over by heroes among men, who were capable of fighting with the greatest care, were smitten down with hundreds of arrows shot by the son of Pritha. Along with these the foremost of heroes among men fell down.

data.v: पद्मार्कपूर्णेन्दुसमाननानि; किरीटमालामुकुटोत्कटानि । भल्लार्धचन्द्रक्षुरहिंसितानि; प्रपेतुरुर्व्यां नृशिरांस्यजस्रम् ॥
data.md: The heads of persons, furnished with faces resembling the lotus, the sun and the full moon in beauty and adorned with diadems, crowns of highest splendour and again, slain by the broad-headed, the crescent-shaped and razorlike arrows, fell down upon the earth without cessation.

data.md: Thereupon the heroes, belonging to the races, called the Kalingas, the Bangas, the Angas and the Nishadhas, most desirous of slaying him, riding upon elephants as splendid as the elephant of the great enemy of the Daityas, proceeded most rapidly against the son of Pandu, who had checked the pride of the foes of the celestials.

data.v: तेषां द्विपानां विचकर्त पार्थो; वर्माणि मर्माणि करान्नियन्तॄन् । ध्वजाः पताकाश्च ततः प्रपेतु;र्वज्राहतानीव गिरेः शिरांसि ॥
data.md: The son of Pritha severed into fragments, the armour, the vital parts, the trunks, the riders, the standards and flags of those elephants, which then fell down upon the earth, even as the summits of mountains drop down on the ground, when smitten by the thunder.

data.v: तेषु प्ररुग्णेषु गुरोस्तनूजं; बाणैः किरीटी नवसूर्यवर्णैः । प्रच्छादयामास महाभ्रजालै;र्वायुः समुद्युक्तमिवांशुमन्तम् ॥
data.md: When that elephant force was entirely destroyed, the diadem-decked one (Arjuna) closed the son of his preceptor with arrows, having the color of the newly-risen sun; even as the wind wholly covers the risen sun with the net-work of vast masses of clouds.

data.v: ततोऽर्जुनेषूनिषुभिर्निरस्य; द्रौणिः शरैरर्जुनवासुदेवौ । प्रच्छादयित्व दिवि चन्द्रसूर्यौ; ननाद सोऽम्भोद इवातपान्ते ॥
data.md: Then having restrained the shafts of Arjuna with the arrows of his own, the son of Drona after closing both Arjuna and Vasudeva with innumerable shafts, roared most loudly; even as the vast mass of clouds, appearing in the firmament at the end of the summer season, after covering both the sun and the moon, makes a loud uproar.

data.md: Arjuna having been highly oppressed with those weapons and having dispelled the darkness (caused with the arrowy showers of Ashvaithaman), suddenly darkened all with the torrents of arrows and again and again pierced him (Ashvatthaman) and all those, belonging to your army, with arrows furnished with the excellent wings.

data.v: संधाय नाराचवरान्दशाशु; द्रौणिस्त्वरन्नेकमिवोत्ससर्ज । तेषां च पञ्चार्जुनमभ्यविध्य;न्पञ्चाच्युतं निर्बिभिदुः सुमुक्ताः ॥
data.md: Then the son of Drona, after having immediately aimed ten foremost of arrows, shot them, as if one with great activity. Of these ten shafts, excellently shot, five pierced Arjuna and the remaining five deeply penetrated that Eternal One (Keshava).

data.md: All the people considered these two foremost of persons, resembling Kubera and Indra, who being struck with those arrows, were drenched in blood (i.e. blood having flowed down their limbs) and who were highly afflicted by that one, who had completed his education (in the science of arms), slain in the field of battle.

data.md: Thereupon the king of the Dasharha race, said to Arjuna these words-Why do you make this mistake? Do you slay this heroic chief. This will, indeed, be committing a great fault, if this person be neglected, who will hereafter be the cause of great uneasiness, even as the disease, if neglected, becomes the cause of great woe.

data.md: The son of Drona, who was thus carried away from the field, on those horses, as swift as the wind, became deeply afflicted with the arrows of the son of Pritha. The most exalted one of the Angirasa's race, who was possessed of immense activity and who became destitute of all aspirations and who had all his arrows and weapons exhausted, after knowing that victory was ever with the chief of the Vrishni race and Dhananjaya, entered into the army of Karna.

data.md: When Ashvatthaman, who was their bitterest enemy, had been carried away by the horses from the field of battle, even as the disease is driven away from the body by incantations, medicines and efficacious means.

data.md: Both Keshava and Arjuna, riding upon cars, with flags waved by the wind and whose rattle was like the loud roar of the clouds, advanced towards the front of the army of the Samsaptakas.

data.md: Sanjaya said Then there had arisen a great uproar, towards the northern part of the Pandava army, amongst the cars, the elephants, the horses and the infantry, as they were being slaughtered by Dandadhara.

data.md: Having turned the course of his car, but not having restrained his horses, that were as swift as either the Gaurda (the chief of the birds) or the wind, Keshava addressed Arjuna, saying

data.md: "The king of the Magadhas of unequalled prowess, who was accompanied by his elephant crushing (his enemies), was not at all inferior to Bhagadatta, either in learning or energy.

data.md: Having slaughtered him (the chief of the Magadhas) at first, do you slay, again the army of the Samsaptakas." Having uttered these words, Keshava carried the son of Pritha to the front of Dandadhara.

data.md: That foremost of the Magadha race, who, like the calamitous planet Ketu amongst all the Planets, was unbearable in managing the elephant-hook, destroyed the army on the side of the antagonist; even as the most dreadful comet destroys the entire earth.

data.md: Having ridden on his elephant, that was furnished with all its equipment's and that was like the Danava with the face and form of an elephant and also that roared like the vast mass of congregated clouds and that had the power of crushing the antagonists, Dandadhara slaughtered thousands of cars, horses and elephants, as well as warriors.

data.md: Having slaughtered the men, who were adorned with the coats of mail made of iron, along with their horses and infantry, he (the chief of the Magadhas) crushed down upon the ground these people by the best and the mightiest of the elephants; even as one crushes the reeds with a sort of crackling sound.

data.md: Thereupon Arjuna, having ridden upon the most handsome car, fell upon that midst of the army, which echoed with the twang of bowstrings, the sound of palms (of hand) and the noise of car-wheels and also was filled with the best and the blard of a large number of cymbals and drums and conches and which, again, was filled with the thousands of cars, horses and elephants.
