data.v: हस्तिदन्तत्सरून्खड्गाञ्जातरूपपरिष्कृतान् । आकीर्णांस्तोमरांश्चापांश्चित्रान्हेमविभूषितान् ॥
वर्माणि चापविद्धानि रुक्मपृष्ठानि भारत । सुवर्णविकृतान्प्रासाञ्शक्तीः कनकभूषिताः ॥
जाम्बूनदमयैः पट्टैर्बद्धाश्च विपुला गदाः । जातरूपमयीश्चर्ष्टीः पट्टिशान्हेमभूषितान् ॥
दण्डैः कनकचित्रैश्च विप्रविद्धान्परश्वधान् । अयस्कुशान्तान्पतितान्मुसलानि गुरूणि च ॥
शतघ्नीः पश्य चित्राश्च विपुलान्परिघांस्तथा । चक्राणि चापविद्धानि मुद्गरांश्च बहून्रणे ॥
नानाविधानि शस्त्राणि प्रगृह्य जयगृद्धिनः । जीवन्त इव लक्ष्यन्ते गतसत्त्वास्तरस्विनः ॥
data.md: The mighty warriors most desirous of victory and possessed of immense activity, after having taken up weapons of diverse kinds, although dead, still looked as if they were living.

data.v: गदाविमथितैर्गात्रैर्मुसलैर्भिन्नमस्तकान् । गजवाजिरथक्षुण्णान्पश्य योधान्सहस्रशः ॥
data.md: Behold those thousands of warriors, who had their limbs crushed by the maces and who had their heads severed by the Mushalas and again, who were highly pressed by the elephants, horses and cars.

data.v: मनुष्यगजवाजीनां शरशक्त्यृष्टितोमरैः । निस्त्रिंशैः पट्टिशैः प्रासैर्नखरैर्लगुडैरपि ॥
data.md: O destroyer of foes, the fields of battle were scattered over the dead bodies of the elephants, horses and men, that had been torn into fragments with the shafts, the arrows called Sakti, swords and lances and scimitars, axes, spears and the Nakharas and clubs; and also those bodies were sineared with the torrents of blood.

data.v: शरीरैर्बहुधा भिन्नैः शोणितौघपरिप्लुतैः । गतासुभिरमित्रघ्न संवृता रणभूमयः ॥
data.md: O destroyer of foes, the fields of battle were scattered over the dead bodies of the elephants, horses and men, that had been torn into fragments with the shafts, the arrows called Sakti, swords and lances and scimitars, axes, spears and the Nakharas and clubs; and also those bodies were sineared with the torrents of blood.

data.v: बाहुभिश्चन्दनादिग्धैः साङ्गदैः शुभभूषणैः । सतलत्रैः सकेयूरैर्भाति भारत मेदिनी ॥
data.md: O descendant of the Bharata race, the earth shines most brilliantly with the arms scattered over her, that are smeared with the soft sandal and that are ornamented with the Angadas and also that are marked with the auspicious signs and that are furnished with the leathern protections and that are adorned with the Keyuras.

data.v: साङ्गुलित्रैर्भुजाग्रैश्च विप्रविद्धैरलंकृतैः । हस्तिहस्तोपमैश्छिन्नैरूरुभिश्च तरस्विनाम् ॥
data.md: (Again, the earth looks most resplendent), strewn over with the hands furnished with the well-protected fingers, severed from their arms and adorned with innumerable ornaments and also with the thighs severed from their bodies and resembling the trunks of elephants and again, with the heads of the most skillful and active warriors, that are adorned with the turbans set with the most valuable gems and furnished with the handsome ear-rings.

data.v: बद्धचूडामणिवरैः शिरोभिश्च सकुण्डलैः । निकृत्तैर्वृषभाक्षाणां विराजति वसुंधरा ॥
कबन्धैः शोणितादिग्धैश्छिन्नगात्रशिरोधरैः । भूर्भाति भरतश्रेष्ठ शान्तार्चिर्भिरिवाग्निभिः ॥
रथान्बहुविधान्भग्नान्हेमकिङ्किणिनः शुभान् । अश्वांश्च बहुधा पश्य शोणितेन परिप्लुतान् ॥
योधानां च महाशङ्खान्पाण्डुरांश्च प्रकीर्णकान् । निरस्तजिह्वान्मातङ्गाञ्शयानान्पर्वतोपमान् ॥
वैजयन्तीविचित्रांश्च हतांश्च गजयोधिनः । वारणानां परिस्तोमान्सुयुक्ताम्बरकम्बलान् ॥
data.md: (Also behold) the variegated the triumphal banners and the elephants, warriors, slain in the battle, the beautiful coverlets of elephants; and the innumerable blankets with excellent (needle) workmanship.

data.v: विपाटिता विचित्राश्च रूपचित्राः कुथास्तथा । भिन्नाश्च बहुधा घण्टाः पतद्भिश्चूर्णिता गजैः ॥
data.md: (Moreover behold) the blankets, that are most handsome, variegated and torn into fragments and as well as the bells, broken into minute particles by the falling elephants and loosened from their bodies.

data.v: वैडूर्यमणिदण्डांश्च पतितानङ्कुशान्भुवि । बद्धाः सादिध्वजाग्रेषु सुवर्णविकृताः कशाः ॥
विचित्रान्मणिचित्रांश्च जातरूपपरिष्कृतान् । अश्वास्तरपरिस्तोमान्राङ्कवान्पतितान्भुवि ॥
data.md: (Behold) the coverlets of horses upon their backs lying upon the ground, that are most beautiful and that are set with the precious jewels and that are adorned with gold and made of the skins of Ranku (a kind of deer).

data.v: चूडामणीन्नरेन्द्राणां विचित्राः काञ्चनस्रजः । छत्राणि चापविद्धानि चामरव्यजनानि च ॥
data.md: (Behold) the headgears of the lords of men and the beautiful garlands made of gold and the umbrellas fallen from their proper places and also the white yak-tails and fans.

data.v: चन्द्रनक्षत्रभासैश्च वदनैश्चारुकुण्डलैः । कॢप्तश्मश्रुभिरत्यर्थं वीराणां समलंकृतैः । वदनैः पश्य संछन्नां महीं शोणितकर्दमाम् ॥
data.md: (Behold) the earth scattered over with the faces, that resemble either the moon or the stars in splendour and that are furnished with handsome ear-rings and that are ornamented with well-cut bcards and that are as brilliant as the full moon.

data.v: सजीवांश्च नरान्पश्य कूजमानान्समन्ततः । उपास्यमानान्बहुभिर्न्यस्तशस्त्रैर्विशां पते ॥
ज्ञातिभिः सहितैस्तत्र रोदमानैर्मुहुर्मुहुः । व्युत्क्रान्तानपरान्योधांश्छादयित्वा तरस्विनः । पुनर्युद्धाय गच्छन्ति जयगृद्धाः प्रमन्यवः ॥
अपरे तत्र तत्रैव परिधावन्ति मानिनः । ज्ञातिभिः पतितैः शूरैर्याच्यमानास्तथोदकम् ॥
जलार्थं च गताः केचिन्निष्प्राणा बहवोऽर्जुन । संनिवृत्ताश्च ते शूरास्तान्दृष्ट्वैव विचेतसः ॥
जलं दृष्ट्वा प्रधावन्ति क्रोशमानाः परस्परम् । जलं पीत्वा मृतान्पश्य पिबतोऽन्यांश्च भारत ॥
परित्यज्य प्रियानन्ये बान्धवान्बान्धवप्रिय । व्युत्क्रान्ताः समदृश्यन्त तत्र तत्र महारणे ॥
पश्यापरान्नरश्रेष्ठ संदष्टौष्ठपुटान्पुनः । भ्रुकुटीकुटिलैर्वक्त्रैः प्रेक्षमाणान्समन्ततः ॥
एतत्तवैवानुरूपं कर्मार्जुन महाहवे । दिवि वा देवराजस्य त्वया यत्कृतमाहवे ॥
data.md: O Arjuna, deeds that had been wrought by you today in this dreadful battle are proper for you, or for the lord of the celestials in heaven.

data.v: एवं तां दर्शयन्कृष्णो युद्धभूमिं किरीटिने । गच्छन्नेवाशृणोच्छब्दं दुर्योधनबले महत् ॥
data.md: While Krishna was thus showing that field of battle to the diadem-decked Arjuna and going to their camp, he heard a loud roar in the army of Duryodhana. (In the army of Duryodhana were heard) the blare of conches and the best of drums and cymbals and the rattle of elephants and the dreadful class of innumerable weapons.

data.v: शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषान्भेरीपणवमिश्रितान् । रथाश्वगजनादांश्च शस्त्रशब्दांश्च दारुणान् ॥
प्रविश्य तद्बलं कृष्णस्तुरगैर्वातवेगिभिः । पाण्ड्येनाभ्यर्दितां सेनां त्वदीयां वीक्ष्य धिष्ठितः ॥
data.md: Having entered that army with horses swift as the wind and also having seen your force crushed down by the chief of the Pandayas, Krishna became highly astonished,

data.v: स हि नानाविधैर्बाणैरिष्वासप्रवरो युधि । न्यहनद्द्विषतां व्रातान्गतासूनन्तको यथा ॥
data.md: That foremost of heroes, who was skilled in the management of arrows and weapons in battle, slaughtered large throngs of enemies with different kinds of shafts, even as Yama (Death) destroys the creatures, deprived of their lives.

data.v: गजवाजिमनुष्याणां शरीराणि शितैः शरैः । भित्त्वा प्रहरतां श्रेष्ठो विदेहासूंश्चकार सः ॥
data.md: That foremost of smiters, after having penetrated the bodies of the elephants, horses and soldiers, with keen arrows, had struck down the foes, who were deprived of both their bodies and lives.

data.v: शत्रुप्रवीरैरस्तानि नानाशस्त्राणि सायकैः । भित्त्वा तानहनत्पाण्ड्यः शत्रूञ्शक्र इवासुरान् ॥
data.md: Then the chief of the Pandavas after having cut-off the innumerable offensive weapons shot by the most dreadful of his enemies with his own arrows had slaughtered those enemies, even as Shakra had slain the Asuras (in the battle of old).

data.v: प्रोक्तस्त्वया पूर्वमेव प्रवीरो लोकविश्रुतः । न त्वस्य कर्म संग्रामे त्वया संजय कीर्तितम् ॥
data.md: Dhritarashtra said The name of that foremost of heroes celebrated all over the world, was related by you already; but O Sanjaya, his achievements in battle were not related by you.

data.v: तस्य विस्तरतो ब्रूहि प्रवीरस्याद्य विक्रमम् । शिक्षां प्रभावं वीर्यं च प्रमाणं दर्पमेव च ॥
data.md: Describe to me detail the prowess, learning, spirit, energy, the amount of strength and pride of that best of heroic warriors.

data.v: द्रोणभीष्मकृपद्रौणिकर्णार्जुनजनार्दनान् । समाप्तविद्यान्धनुषि श्रेष्ठान्यान्मन्यसे युधि ॥
data.md: Sanjaya said You raged Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, the son of Drona, Karna, Arjuna and Janardana to be well versed in the knowledge of weapons and also to be the foremost of all bowmen and again, the best of car-warriors.

data.v: तुल्यता कर्णभीष्माभ्यामात्मनो येन दृश्यते । वासुदेवार्जुनाभ्यां च न्यूनतां नात्मनीच्छति ॥
data.md: He (Pandya) does not admit that he cqual to either Karna or Bhishma; nor docs he wish that he is inferior to Vasudeva or Arjuna.

data.v: स पाण्ड्यो नृपतिश्रेष्ठः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः । कर्णस्यानीकमवधीत्परिभूत इवान्तकः ॥
data.md: That foremost of kings, Pandaya, who was the most superior to all that are versed in the management of all weapons, slaughtered the army of Karna, even as highly insulted Death destroys all the creatures.

data.v: तदुदीर्णरथाश्वं च पत्तिप्रवरकुञ्जरम् । कुलालचक्रवद्भ्रान्तं पाण्ड्येनाधिष्ठितं बलम् ॥
data.md: That army (of Karna), which teemed with innumerable cars and horses, as also with the most expert of foot-soldiers, having been smitten down by Pandya, circled round like the wheel of the potter.

data.v: व्यश्वसूतध्वजरथान्विप्रविद्धायुधान्रिपून् । सम्यगस्तैः शरैः पाण्ड्यो वायुर्मेघानिवाक्षिपत् ॥
data.md: Pandya had, with his excellently-shot arrows, continued to scatter about that force, slaughtering its horses, drivers, standards and cars, as also displacing its weapons and striking down its elephants, even as the wind disperses the masses of clouds.

data.v: द्विरदान्प्रहतप्रोथान्विपताकध्वजायुधान् । सपादरक्षानवधीद्वज्रेणारीनिवारिहा ॥
data.md: He (Pandya) had slaughtered the elephants along with their riders and foot-soldiers guarding them and had split asunder the banners, weapons and standards (with which they were equipt) of that army; even as the breaker of mountains splits as under the mountains with the thunder-bolt.

data.v: सशक्तिप्रासतूणीरानश्वारोहान्हयानपि । पुलिन्दखशबाह्लीकान्निषादान्ध्रकतङ्गणान् ॥
दाक्षिणात्यांश्च भोजांश्च क्रूरान्संग्रामकर्कशान् । विशस्त्रकवचान्बाणैः कृत्वा पाण्ड्योऽकरोद्व्यसून् ॥
data.md: He had smitten down the horses as well as the horsemen, who were armed with the arrows called Sakti, the lances and quivers. And then had destroyed the lives of the Pulindas, the Khasas, the Balhikas, the Nishadhas, the Andhakas, the Tanganas, the Southerners and the Bhojas, who were all possessed of heroism and very hardly and obstinate in the field of battle, after having deprived them of their weapons and coats of armour, by means of innumerable arrows.

data.v: चतुरङ्गं बलं बाणैर्निघ्नन्तं पाण्ड्यमाहवे । दृष्ट्वा द्रौणिरसंभ्रान्तमसंभ्रान्ततरोऽभ्ययात् ॥
data.md: Having seen that Pandya in the field was slaughtering the army consisting of the four principal elements by means of his shafts, then the son of Drona, undaunted with fear, advanced against that fearless warrior.

data.v: आभाष्य चैनं मधुरमभि नृत्यन्नभीतवत् । प्राह प्रहरतां श्रेष्ठः स्मितपूर्वं समाह्वयन् ॥
data.md: Having fearlessly addressed this hero (Pandya) in sweet words, who was then supposed to dance (on his car, in the field of battle) and also having called him to battle with a smiling face, that foremost of smiters (the son

data.v: राजन्कमलपत्राक्ष प्रधानायुधवाहन । वज्रसंहननप्रख्य प्रधानबलपौरुष ॥
data.md: “O monarch, O you, who art possessed of eyes like the petals of a louts. O you of high parentage, O you who art versed in all the sciences, O you who do resemble the mightest smiter of the thunder-bolt. (Indra), O you, whose strength and prowess are most noted.

data.v: मुष्टिश्लिष्टायुधाभ्यां च व्यायताभ्यां महद्धनुः । दोर्भ्यां विस्फारयन्भासि महाजलदवद्भृशम् ॥
data.md: Having caught the long bow-string in your grasp and stretched the bow by your two massive arms and also having pulled it by your hands, you look most handsome like a mass of congregated clouds.

data.v: शरवर्षैर्महावेगैरमित्रानभिवर्षतः । मदन्यं नानुपश्यामि प्रतिवीरं तवाहवे ॥
data.md: You have continued pouring down showers of arrows, possessed of great impetuosity. I do not find any other hero than myself who can stand against you in the field of battle.

data.v: रथद्विरदपत्त्यश्वानेकः प्रमथसे बहून् । मृगसंघानिवारण्ये विभीर्भीमबलो हरिः ॥
data.md: Being alone, you smite down innumerable cars, elephants, foot-soldiers and horses; even as the fearless lion of undaunted prowess kills a large number of deer in the forest.

data.v: महता रथघोषेण दिवं भूमिं च नादयन् । वर्षान्ते सस्यहा पीथो भाभिरापूरयन्निव ॥
data.md: Having made both the firmament and the earth resound with the great rattle of your carwheels, you look look most resplendent, O monarch, like the congregated mass of clouds, that destroys all the crops appearing at the end of the rains and making loud roars.

data.v: संस्पृशानः शरांस्तीक्ष्णांस्तूणादाशीविषोपमान् । मयैवैकेन युध्यस्व त्र्यम्बकेणान्धको यथा ॥
data.md: Having taken out your sharp arrows from the quiver, that are like the snakes of virulent poison, do you fight with me alone; even as Andhaka (Asura) fought with the three-eyed deity (Shiva) (in the days of yore).

data.v: एवमुक्तस्तथेत्युक्त्वा प्रहरेति च ताडितः । कर्णिना द्रोणतनयं विव्याध मलयध्वजः ॥
data.md: Having been thus addressed by the son of Drona and uttering these words-So be it and also strike, Malayadhvaja was greatly assailed and he (Pandya) himself in return pierced the son of Drona with a barbed arrow.

data.v: मर्मभेदिभिरत्युग्रैर्बाणैरग्निशिखोपमैः । स्मयन्नभ्यहनद्द्रौणिः पाण्ड्यमाचार्यसत्तमः ॥
data.md: Thereupon the son of Drona, that foremost of preceptors, had smilingly struck down Pandya with numerous arrows, that penetrate even the vitals and also that are possessed of great impetuosity and again, that resemble the flames of fire in splendour.

data.v: ततो नवापरांस्तीक्ष्णान्नाराचान्कङ्कवाससः । गत्या दशम्या संयुक्तानश्वत्थामा व्यवासृजत् ॥
data.md: Thereafter Ashvatthaman, too, shot (at his enemy) several other broad-headed arrows, that are furnished with sharp points and that are capable of penetrating the very vitals and also that are possessed of ten different motions.

data.v: तेषां पञ्चाच्छिनत्पाण्ड्यः पञ्चभिर्निशितैः शरैः । चत्वारोऽभ्याहनन्वाहानाशु ते व्यसवोऽभवन् ॥
data.md: Then Pandya severed those arrows (of his antagonist) by means of his nine keen shafts; and by means of four other arrows he afflicted the horses (four in number), that had immediately been deprived of their lives.

data.v: अथ द्रोणसुतस्येषूंस्तांश्छित्त्वा निशितैः शरैः । धनुर्ज्यां विततां पाण्ड्यश्चिच्छेदादित्यवर्चसः ॥
data.md: Thereupon, having struck down those arrows of the son of Drona, that had the splendour of the sun, with his own keen shafts, pandya cut-off the stretched bowstring (of his antagonist),

data.v: विज्यं धनुरथाधिज्यं कृत्वा द्रौणिरमित्रहा । ततः शरसहस्राणि प्रेषयामास पाण्ड्यतः । इषुसंबाधमाकाशमकरोद्दिश एव च ॥
data.md: That twice-born person then sent away thousands of arrows (upon his antagonist); and he thereby filled the entire firmament and the different points of the horizon with his shafts.

data.v: ततस्तानस्यतः सर्वान्द्रौणेर्बाणान्महात्मनः । जानानोऽप्यक्षयान्पाण्ड्योऽशातयत्पुरुषर्षभः ॥
data.md: Having been conscious of the fact that all those arrows of the high-souled son of Drona shot by himself, were, indeed, inexhaustible, that foremost of persons. Pandya, then cut them all into fragments.

data.v: प्रहितांस्तान्प्रयत्नेन छित्त्वा द्रौणेरिषूनरिः । चक्ररक्षौ ततस्तस्य प्राणुदन्निशितैः शरैः ॥
data.md: Then, again the antagonist of the son of Drona, after having severed those arrows shot (by his foe) most carefully, had slain in the battle the two protectors of his (enemy's) carwheels, by means of his own keen shafts.

data.v: अथारेर्लाघवं दृष्ट्वा मण्डलीकृतकार्मुकः । प्रास्यद्द्रोणसुतो बाणान्वृष्टिं पूषानुजो यथा ॥
data.md: Thereupon having observed the lightness of hand of his antagonist, the son of Drona had stringed his bow into a circle and shot innumerable arrows, even as the mass of clouds pours down the torrents of rain.

data.v: अष्टावष्टगवान्यूहुः शकटानि यदायुधम् । अह्नस्तदष्टभागेन द्रौणिश्चिक्षेप मारिष ॥
data.md: O sire, the son of Drona shot, within the eighth part of a day, as many weapons as could be conveyed in eight cars drawn by eight bullocks.

data.v: तमन्तकमिव क्रुद्धमन्तकालान्तकोपमम् । ये ये ददृशिरे तत्र विसंज्ञाः प्रायशोऽभवन् ॥
data.md: Almost all those people, whoever behold him (Ashvatthaman), who then looked like the highly enraged Death himself, who resembled the very destroyer of Death himself, had wholly lost their senses.

data.v: पर्जन्य इव घर्मान्ते वृष्ट्या साद्रिद्रुमां महीम् । आचार्यपुत्रस्तां सेनां बाणवृष्ट्याभ्यवीवृषत् ॥
data.md: The son of the preceptor poured froth showers of arrows upon that hostile army, even as the mass of congregated clouds, at the expiration of the summer, drops down showers of rain upon the earth, containing mountains and trees upon her.

data.v: द्रौणिपर्जन्यमुक्तां तां बाणवृष्टिं सुदुःसहाम् । वायव्यास्त्रेण स क्षिप्रं रुद्ध्वा पाण्ड्यानिलोऽनदत् ॥
data.md: Then Pandya, who was like the wind, after having checked, with his weapon, called the or Vayavya, that intolerable shower of shafts poured down by the son of Drona, who was like the mass of clouds, roared most loudly with great gratification.

data.v: तस्य नानदतः केतुं चन्दनागुरुभूषितम् । मलयप्रतिमं द्रौणिश्छित्त्वाश्वांश्चतुरोऽहनत् ॥
data.md: The son of Drona, after having cut-off the standards, that was smcared with soft sandal and paste of Agura and also that resembled the Malaya inountain, of that person, who uttered inost loud roars, slaughtered four horses (belonging to him-Pandya).

data.v: सूतमेकेषुणा हत्वा महाजलदनिस्वनम् । धनुश्छित्त्वार्धचन्द्रेण व्यधमत्तिलशो रथम् ॥
data.md: After having slaughtered his (Pandya's) charioteer with a single arrow and also having severed his bow, that twanged like a vast mass of clouds, with a crescent-shaped arrow, had broken down his car into smallest fragments.

data.v: अस्त्रैरस्त्राणि संवार्य छित्त्वा सर्वायुधानि च । प्राप्तमप्यहितं द्रौणिर्न जघान रणेप्सया ॥
data.md: Having restrained the weapons (shot by his antagonist) by the weapons of his own and also having struck down all these weapons, the son of Drona, most desirous of encountering (with his foe), did not slaughter him even on receiving his antagonist (within his reach).

data.v: हतेश्वरो दन्तिवरः सुकल्पित;स्त्वराभिसृष्टः प्रतिशर्मगो बली । तमध्यतिष्ठन्मलयेश्वरो महा;न्यथाद्रिशृङ्गं हरिरुन्नदंस्तथा ॥
स तोमरं भास्कररश्मिसंनिभं; बलास्त्रसर्गोत्तमयत्नमन्युभिः । ससर्ज शीघ्रं प्रतिपीडयन्गजं; गुरोः सुतायाद्रिपतीश्वरो नदन् ॥
data.md: Being highly enraged and most careful in the matter of hurling weapons with great impctuosity, that lord of the prince of mountains, roaring most loudly and afflicting the elephant, had hurled immediately a lance, that had the splendour of the rays of the sun, towards the son of the preceptor.

data.v: मणिप्रतानोत्तमवज्रहाटकै;रलंकृतं चांशुकमाल्यमौक्तिकैः । हतोऽस्यसावित्यसकृन्मुदा नद;न्पराभिनद्द्रौणिवराङ्गभूषणम् ॥
data.md: Having shouted with joy, uttering repeatedly-You are slain, you are slain, he (Pandya) broke into pieces the diadem of the son of Drona, that was ornamented with the best sorts of jewels and furnished with the superior kinds of diamonds and again, equipt with first-class gold and excellent cloths and garlands of pearls.

data.v: तदर्कचन्द्रग्रहपावकत्विषं; भृशाभिघातात्पतितं विचूर्णितम् । महेन्द्रवज्राभिहतं महावनं; यथाद्रिशृङ्गं धरणीतले तथा ॥
data.md: The diadem, that was resplendent as either the sun, or the moon, or the planets, or the fire, fell down on account of the severe stroke and was broken into minute fragments; even as the summit of a mountain, smitten by the thunder of Indra, falls upon the face of the earth, sending forth a very great noise.

data.v: ततः प्रजज्वाल परेण मन्युना; पदाहतो नागपतिर्यथा तथा । समादधे चान्तकदण्डसंनिभा;निषूनमित्रान्तकरांश्चतुर्दश ॥
data.md: Thereupon he (the son of Drona), became fiery with great wrath, even as the king of the snakes, being trodden down by the foot, blazes forth with anger. He then took up fourteen shafts, that resembled the rod of Death himself and also that were capable of afflicting the enemies.

data.v: द्विपस्य पादाग्रकरान्स पञ्चभि;र्नृपस्य बाहू च शिरोऽथ च त्रिभिः । जघान षड्भिः षडृतूत्तमत्विषः; स पाण्ड्यराजानुचरान्महारथान् ॥
data.md: He then cut-off the (four) feet and trunk of that elephant (belonging to his antagonist) with five arrows, as well as the arms and head of the king with three other shafts; and thereafter he siaughtered the nighty car-warriors, who accompanied king Pandya to the field and who, again, were highly resplendent.

data.v: सुदीर्घवृत्तौ वरचन्दनोक्षितौ; सुवर्णमुक्तामणिवज्रभूषितौ । भुजौ धरायां पतितौ नृपस्य तौ; विवेष्टतुस्तार्क्ष्यहताविवोरगौ ॥
data.md: Those two arms of the king, that were pretty long and round and that were smeared with excellent sandal past and also that were ornamented with gold, pearls, gems and diamonds, rolled on, falling upon the earth, like two snakes slain by Garuda.

data.v: शिरश्च तत्पूर्णशशिप्रभाननं; सरोषताम्रायतनेत्रमुन्नसम् । क्षितौ विबभ्राज पतत्सकुण्डलं; विशाखयोर्मध्यगतः शशी यथा ॥
data.md: The head, again, that was furnished with a face resembling the full moon and with eyes, large and red like copper, on account of wrath and that had a prominent nose and also that was adorned with the ear-rings, blazed upon the earth, even as the moon shines between two constellations.

data.v: समाप्तविद्यं तु गुरोः सुतं नृपः; समाप्तकर्माणमुपेत्य ते सुतः । सुहृद्वृतोऽत्यर्थमपूजयन्मुदा; जिते बलौ विष्णुमिवामरेश्वरः ॥
data.md: Then king, your son, after having advanced towards him, most joyfully worshipped, with enough of reverence, the son of the preceptor, who had finished all learning and who, again, had completed all his tasks, while (the king) was himself surrounded by all his brothers; as the lord of the celestials most cheerfully worshipped Vishnu after the subjugation of Bali (an Asura). even

data.v: पाण्ड्ये हते किमकरोदर्जुनो युधि संजय । एकवीरेण कर्णेन द्रावितेषु परेषु च ॥
data.md: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, on the slaughter of Pandya and also while that foremost of warriors, Karna, destroyed the hostile force, what did Arjuna do in the field of battle?

data.v: समाप्तविद्यो बलवान्युक्तो वीरश्च पाण्डवः । सर्वभूतेष्वनुज्ञातः शंकरेण महात्मना ॥
data.md: That son of Pandu, who had finished the study of all sciences and who also was possessed of immense strength and who was attentive to fixed duties and who was a hero, was made by the lofty-minded Sankara most invincible amongst all creatures.

data.v: तस्मान्महद्भयं तीव्रममित्रघ्नाद्धनंजयात् । स यत्तत्राकरोत्पार्थस्तन्ममाचक्ष्व संजय ॥
data.md: My greatest and highly tormenting terrors from that slayer slayer of antagonists, Dhananjaya. O Sanjaya, do you relate to me in detail what the son of Pritha had done there on that on that occasion. are

data.v: हते पाण्ड्येऽर्जुनं कृष्णस्त्वरन्नाह वचो हितम् । पश्यातिमान्यं राजानमपयातांश्च पाण्डवान् ॥
data.md: Sanjaya said On the death of Pandya, Krishna, with great activity, uttered these most beneficial words to Arjuna-'I do not find out the king. The other Pandavas have fled away (from the field of battle).'

data.v: अश्वत्थाम्नश्च संकल्पाद्धताः कर्णेन सृञ्जयाः । तथाश्वनरनागानां कृतं च कदनं महत् । इत्याचष्ट सुदुर्धर्षो वासुदेवः किरीटिने ॥
एतच्छ्रुत्वा च दृष्ट्वा च भ्रातुर्घोरं महद्भयम् । वाहयाश्वान्हृषीकेश क्षिप्रमित्याह पाण्डवः ॥
data.md: Hearing of the great and immense fear of his brother (Yudhishthira), as also witnessing it, the Pandava readily addressed him thus-'O Hrishikesha, urge the horses.'

data.v: ततः प्रायाद्धृषीकेशो रथेनाप्रतियोधिना । दारुणश्च पुनस्तत्र प्रादुरासीत्समागमः ॥
data.md: Thereupon, Hrishikesha went (to the battle), ascending on an irresistible car. Then there raged a dreadful battle.

data.v: ततः प्रववृते भूयः संग्रामो राजसत्तम । कर्णस्य पाण्डवानां च यमराष्ट्रविवर्धनः ॥
data.md: Thereupon, O best of monarchs, again the dreadful battle took place between Karna and Pandavas, which aggrandised the kingdom of Yama.

data.v: धनूंषि बाणान्परिघानसितोमरपट्टिशान् । मुसलानि भुशुण्डीश्च शक्तिऋष्टिपरश्वधान् ॥
गदाः प्रासानसीन्कुन्तान्भिण्डिपालान्महाङ्कुशान् । प्रगृह्य क्षिप्रमापेतुः परस्परजिगीषया ॥
बाणज्यातलशब्देन द्यां दिशः प्रदिशो वियत् । पृथिवीं नेमिघोषेण नादयन्तोऽभ्ययुः परान् ॥
data.md: Having filled the firmament, the ten different points of the horison as well as the other subsidiary subsidiary points points and and the upper atmosphere with the noise of arrows, the bowstring and the sound of palms and again, having made the entire earth echo with the noise of clatter car-wheels, the warriors proceeded against their antagonists.

data.v: तेन शब्देन महता संहृष्टाश्चक्रुराहवम् । वीरा वीरैर्महाघोरं कलहान्तं तितीर्षवः ॥
data.md: Being gratified with that tremendous noise, the hero, who were most willing to cross over and reach the shore of that dreadful ocean of hostility, began to fight with numerous other horses.

data.v: ज्यातलत्रधनुःशब्दाः कुञ्जराणां च बृंहितम् । ताडितानां च पततां निनादः सुमहानभूत् ॥
data.md: There was a great noise of the bowstrings, bows and lances and the loud roar of elephants; as also there were terrible shouts of the foot soldiers and men falling (upon the earth).

data.v: बाणशब्दांश्च विविधाञ्शूराणामभिगर्जताम् । श्रुत्वा शब्दं भृशं त्रेसुर्जघ्नुर्मम्लुश्च भारत ॥
data.md: There, having heard the numerous kinds of arrow sounds and the terrible uproar of the heroic warriors, the combatants were deeply struck with terror, fell down and became very pale.

data.v: तेषां नानद्यतां चैव शस्त्रवृष्टिं च मुञ्चताम् । बहूनाधिरथिः कर्णः प्रममाथ रणेषुभिः ॥
data.md: The warlike son of Adhiratha crushed, with innumerable arrows, large numbers of these enemies, who uttered loud roars and poured forth showers of weapons.

data.v: पञ्च पाञ्चालवीराणां रथान्दश च पञ्च च । साश्वसूतध्वजान्कर्णः शरैर्निन्ये यमक्षयम् ॥
data.md: Then Karna led to the abode of Death twenty car-warriors against the Panchala heroes, along with their horses, drivers and standards, by means of his innumerable arrows.

data.v: योधमुख्या महावीर्याः पाण्डूनां कर्णमाहवे । शीघ्रास्त्रा दिवमावृत्य परिवव्रुः समन्ततः ॥
data.md: Then, again, the best of the warriors of the vast Pandava force, who were all very powerful and who also were very sinart in the management of weapons, after having careered round, surrounded Karna from all sides in the field of battle.

data.v: ततः कर्णो द्विषत्सेनां शरवर्षैर्विलोडयन् । विजगाहेऽण्डजापूर्णां पद्मिनीमिव यूथपः ॥
data.md: Thereupon Karna crushed the army belonging to the foes by means of showers of shafts; even as the leader of the elephants, plunging into a lake, crushes down the lotuses and swans, adorning the lake itself.

data.v: द्विषन्मध्यमवस्कन्द्य राधेयो धनुरुत्तमम् । विधुन्वानः शितैर्बाणैः शिरांस्युन्मथ्य पातयत् ॥
data.md: The son of Radha, after having entered the hostile force and also having shaken his best of bonds had struck off their heads with his keen arrows and caused them to fall upon the carth.

data.v: चर्मवर्माणि संछिन्द्य निर्वापमिव देहिनाम् । विषेहुर्नास्य संपर्कं द्वितीयस्य पतत्रिणः ॥
data.md: Being broken into pieces, the shields and coats of mail, belonging to the warriors, fell upon the earth; and none of them could bear the touch of a second arrow (to be shot by Karna).

data.v: वर्मदेहासुमथनैर्धनुषः प्रच्युतैः शरैः । मौर्व्या तलत्रैर्न्यवधीत्कशया वाजिनो यथा ॥
data.md: He (Karna) struck the fences of the antagonists, that could be perceivable only by the bowstrings, by means of shafts shot from his bow, that were capable of crushing the coats of mail, the bodies and the lives of the combatants); even as one strikes the horses with the whip.

data.v: पाण्डुसृञ्जयपाञ्चालाञ्शरगोचरमानयत् । ममर्द कर्णस्तरसा सिंहो मृगगणानिव ॥
data.md: Then Karna, with great speed, crushed down the Pandus, the Panchalas and the Srinjayas, who came with the reach of his arrows; even as the lion slays the whole lot of dear.

data.v: ततः पाञ्चालपुत्राश्च द्रौपदेयाश्च मारिष । यमौ च युयुधानश्च सहिताः कर्णमभ्ययुः ॥
data.md: Thereupon, O sire, the king of the Panchalas, the sons of Draupadi, the twin brothers and Yuyudhana, who all gathered together, advanced against Karna.

data.v: व्यायच्छमानाः सुभृशं कुरुपाण्डवसृञ्जयाः । प्रियानसून्रणे त्यक्त्वा योधा जग्मुः परस्परम् ॥
data.md: Whilst the Kurus, the Panchalas and the Pandus were fighting with one another, the combatants, offering up their lives slaughtered one another in the field of battle.

data.v: सुसंनद्धाः कवचिनः सशिरस्त्राणभूषणाः । गदाभिर्मुसलैश्चान्ये परिघैश्च महारथाः ॥
data.md: O sire, the mighty warriors, who were all protected with armours and coats of mail and who also were ornamented with the headgears, uplifting their maces, short clubs and spiked maces, that resembled the very uplifted rod of Death jumped, marched most rapidly and dreadfully against their antagonists.

data.v: समभ्यधावन्त भृशं देवा दण्डैरिवोद्यतैः । नदन्तश्चाह्वयन्तश्च प्रवल्गन्तश्च मारिष ॥
data.md: O sire, the mighty warriors, who were all protected with armours and coats of mail and who also were ornamented with the headgears, uplifting their maces, short clubs and spiked maces, that resembled the very uplifted rod of Death jumped, marched most rapidly and dreadfully against their antagonists.

data.md: The faces and limbs of the slain rested on the field and O king, the most beautiful forms of the elephants, horses and men, that resembled the dirty cloths, presented an exceedingly gloomy site.

data.md: Sanjaya said Having been persuaded by your son, many elephant-warriors, riding upon their elephants and desiring to bring about his destruction, became highly enraged and marched against Dhristadyumna.

data.md: Many foremost of clephant-warriors belonging to the tribes called the Easterners, the Southerners, the Angas, the Bangas, the Pundras, the Magadhas and the Tamaliptakas.

data.md: And O descendant of the Bharata race, also belonging to the Mekalas, the Koshalas, the Madras, the Dasharnas and the Nishadhas, who were all very skillful in fighting on the back of elephants and who again, were accompanied by the Kalingas.

data.md: He (Dhristadyumna) then dropped down showers of arrows and broad-headed shafts upon those elephants, that crushed down the enemies and also that were urged forward by their being deeply struck in the sides with heels, toes and hooks.

data.md: O descendant of the Bharata race, he (the Panchala chief) pierced every one of these elephants, that resembled mountains with ten, six or eight keen arrows.

data.md: Being driven by the Mlechchas, these elephants, highly enraged, had cast down the men, the horses and cars, with their trunks and crushed them with their feet.

data.md: Shahadeva, on the other hand, had struck the elephant of falling Pundra, that was moving like a mountain, with three long arrows, which were most excellently directed.

data.md: Then Shahadeva, after having deprived that elephant of his banners, driver, armour, standard and life, again advanced against the ruler of the Angas.

data.md: But Nakula, having forbidden Shahadeva (from advancement), himself crushed the chief of the Angas with three long shafts resembling the very rods of Death in appearance, as well as his elephant with hundred others.

data.v: दिवाकरकरप्रख्यानङ्गश्चिक्षेप तोमरान् । नकुलाय शतान्यष्टौ त्रिधैकैकं तु सोऽच्छिनत् ॥
data.md: The ruler of the Angas, on the other hand, had directed eight hundred lances, that were as resplendent as the rays of the sun, towards Nakula, who, again, shattered each of them into three pieces.

data.md: That were adorned with waving banners and also that were furnished with excellent mouths and that were decked with the housings made of gold and that were as resplendent as the blazing mountains; for, the warriors were most desirous of crushing him and all possessed of immense activity.

data.md: Thereupon, the battle raged between the car-warriors, who were shooting showers of shafts and hurling down thousands of lances, (at the antagonists) and the heroes fighting from the back of elephant.

data.md: The frontal globes and several other vitals, the tusks and the equipments of the elephants, that were deeply pierced with long shafts, were all shattered.

data.md: Having been killed with the torrents of shafts by such clouds as the Pandu warriors, those hills of elephants belonging to the foes, fell down; even as the mountains are struck down by the falling of thunders.

data.md: Those warriors, belonging to the side of the son of Pandu, after having first agitated that army and again having afflicted, proceeded most rapidly against Karna.

data.v: सहदेवं ततः क्रुद्धं दहन्तं तव वाहिनीम् । दुःशासनो महाराज भ्राता भ्रातरमभ्ययात् ॥
data.md: Sanjaya said O great monarch, Dushasana rushed against Shahadeva, that is, brother against brother, who was highly enraged and blasted your army.

data.v: तौ समेतौ महायुद्धे दृष्ट्वा तत्र नराधिपाः । सिंहनादरवांश्चक्रुर्वासांस्यादुधुवुश्च ह ॥

data.v: सहदेवस्ततो राजन्नाराचेन तवात्मजम् । विद्ध्वा विव्याध सप्तत्या सारथिं च त्रिभिस्त्रिभिः ॥
data.md: Then, O monarch, Shahadeva, after having first pierced your son, again struck him with seventy shafts, as well as his charioteer with threc others.

data.v: दुःशासनस्तदा राजंश्छित्त्वा चापं महाहवे । सहदेवं त्रिसप्तत्या बाह्वोरुरसि चार्दयत् ॥
data.md: Thereupon, O king, Dushasana, after having severed his bow in that dreadful battle, struck Shahadeva with seventy-three arrows both in the arms and the chest.

data.md: Thus having severed his (Dusasana's) bow along with its string and arrow, then that fearful sword fell down upon the earth, even as a snake falls down from heaven upon the ground.

data.v: अथान्यद्धनुरादाय सहदेवः प्रतापवान् । दुःशासनाय चिक्षेप बाणमन्तकरं ततः ॥
data.md: Thereupon Shahadeva, possessed of immerise prowess, having taken up another bow, hurled at Dushasana a shaft, capable of bringing about death.

data.md: Then the son of Kuru had severed into two fragments, with his keen-edged sword, that shaft, which was as resplendent as the very rod of Death himself, directed towards him.

data.v: तमापतन्तं सहसा निस्त्रिंशं निशितैः शरैः । पातयामास समरे सहदेवो हसन्निव ॥
data.md: On the other hand, Shahadeva, as if laughing, had suddenly thrown down that sword with keen arrows, that was directed towards him.

data.v: ततो बाणांश्चतुःषष्टिं तव पुत्रो महारणे । सहदेवरथे तूर्णं पातयामास भारत ॥
data.md: Thereupon, O descendant of the Bharata race, your son most rapidly directed sixty-four arrows against the car of Shahadeva, in that dreadful battle.

data.v: ताञ्शरान्समरे राजन्वेगेनापततो बहून् । एकैकं पञ्चभिर्बाणैः सहदेवो न्यकृन्तत ॥
data.md: Then Shahadeva, O monarch, cut-off every one of these innumerable arrows, that were falling with speed (upon him) with five shafts of his own in that battle.

data.v: स निवार्य महाबाणांस्तव पुत्रेण प्रेषितान् । अथास्मै सुबहून्बाणान्माद्रीपुत्रः समाचिनोत् ॥
data.md: Having thus restrained those powerful arrows, shot by your son, he (Shahadeva) sent away innumerable shafts against him (his antagonist) in that dreadful battle.

data.v: ततः क्रुद्धो महाराज सहदेवः प्रतापवान् । समाधत्त शरं घोरं मृत्युकालान्तकोपमम् । विकृष्य बलवच्चापं तव पुत्राय सोऽसृजत् ॥
data.md: O mighty monarch, the most powerful Shahadeva, being highly enraged at this, fixed an arrow on his bow, that was as deadly as Death himself.

data.v: स तं निर्भिद्य वेगेन भित्त्वा च कवचं महत् । प्राविशद्धरणीं राजन्वल्मीकमिव पन्नगः । ततः स मुमुहे राजंस्तव पुत्रो महारथः ॥
data.md: Then having stretched his bow with great force, he shot that arrow at your son. O monarch, that shaft, after having successively pierced with great force through his body and his strong armour, itself entered into the earth, even as the snakes enter into the ant-hill. Thereupon, O king, your son, that mighty carwarrior, became senseless.

data.v: मूढं चैनं समालक्ष्य सारथिस्त्वरितो रथम् । अपोवाह भृशं त्रस्तो वध्यमानं शितैः शरैः ॥
data.md: Having seen him thus senseless and himself being deeply struck with sharp arrows, his charioteer with great rapidity carried away the car.

data.v: पराजित्य रणे तं तु पाण्डवः पाण्डुपूर्वज । दुर्योधनबलं हृष्टः प्रामथद्वै समन्ततः ॥
data.md: Having defeated that Kuru warrior in battle, the son of Pandu looked at the army of Duryodhana and crushed it on all sides.

data.v: पिपीलिकापुटं राजन्यथामृद्नान्नरो रुषा । तथा सा कौरवी सेना मृदिता तेन भारत ॥
data.md: O descendant of the Bharata race, O monarch, that force belonging to the Kurus was crushed by the son of Pandu, even as a swarm of ants is crushed to death by a man with great rage.

data.v: नकुलं रभसं युद्धे दारयन्तं वरूथिनीम् । कर्णो वैकर्तनो राजन्वारयामास वै तदा ॥
data.md: Sanjaya said O monarch, Karna the son of Vikartana, indeed, restrained with great rage Nakula, who was destroying and dispersing the army (belonging to the Kurus) in that battle.

data.v: नकुलश्च तदा कर्णं प्रहसन्निदमब्रवीत् । चिरस्य बत दृष्टोऽहं दैवतैः सौम्यचक्षुषा ॥
data.md: Thereupon, Nakula smilingly uttered these words of Karna-'I am, after a long while and through the kindness of the celestials, seen by you.

data.v: यस्य मे त्वं रणे पाप चक्षुर्विषयमागतः । त्वं हि मूलमनर्थानां वैरस्य कलहस्य च ॥
data.md: O wretched one, such as I am, you have become the object of my sight in this battle. Indeed, you are the root of all these evils, as well as of this hostility and warfare.

data.v: त्वद्दोषात्कुरवः क्षीणाः समासाद्य परस्परम् । त्वामद्य समरे हत्वा कृतकृत्योऽस्मि विज्वरः ॥
data.md: Through you faults the Kuru warriors, after having fought against one another had become thinned. Having slaughtered you today in the battle. I will consider myself as having performed my duties; and also I will be free from the fever (of my heart).

data.v: एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच नकुलं सूतनन्दनः । सदृशं राजपुत्रस्य धन्विनश्च विशेषतः ॥
data.md: Being thus addressed, the son of Suta replied to Nakula in expressions worthy of the son of a king and of a bowman specialiy.

data.v: प्रहरस्व रणे बाल पश्यामस्तव पौरुषम् । कर्म कृत्वा रणे शूर ततः कत्थितुमर्हसि ॥
data.md: 'O brave warrior, strike me; we will behold your manliness. O hero, first having achieved some deed in the battle, then it behoves you to speak.

data.v: अनुक्त्वा समरे तात शूरा युध्यन्ति शक्तितः । स युध्यस्व मया शक्त्या विनेष्ये दर्पमद्य ते ॥
data.md: O sire, without speaking anything (highly of themselves) in the battle, the warriors fight to the best of their might. hence, do you fight with me to the best of your power. I will surely destroy your vanity.

data.v: इत्युक्त्वा प्राहरत्तूर्णं पाण्डुपुत्राय सूतजः । विव्याध चैनं समरे त्रिसप्तत्या शिलीमुखैः ॥
data.md: Having addressed him thus, the son of Suta struck the son of Pandu most rapidly and pierced him in the battle with seventy-three arrows.

data.v: नकुलस्तु ततो विद्धः सूतपुत्रेण भारत । अशीत्याशीविषप्रख्यैः सूतपुत्रमविध्यत ॥
data.md: Thereupon, O descendant of the Bharata race, Nakula, indeed, having been thus pierced by the son of Suta, pierced the Suta's son in return with eight shafts, that were as deadly as the snakes possessing virulent poison.

data.v: तस्य कर्णो धनुश्छित्त्वा स्वर्णपुङ्खैः शिलाशितैः । त्रिंशता परमेष्वासः शरैः पाण्डवमार्दयत् ॥
data.md: Then Karna, that most powerful bowman, after having severed his (enemy's) bow with numerous shafts, winged with gold and sharpened on stone, crushed the son of Pandu with thirty other arrows.

data.v: ते तस्य कवचं भित्त्वा पपुः शोणितमाहवे । आशीविषा यथा नागा भित्त्वा गां सलिलं पपुः ॥
data.md: Those arrows, after having pierced through his armour, drank his blood in the battle; even as the snakes of virulent poison, after having penetrated the earth, drink the water.

data.v: अथान्यद्धनुरादाय हेमपृष्ठं दुरासदम् । कर्णं विव्याध विंशत्या सारथिं च त्रिभिः शरैः ॥
data.md: Then he (Nakula), taking up another bow, that was most formidable and adorned with gold on the back, penetrated Karna with twenty shafts and pierced his charioteer with three others.

data.v: ततः क्रुद्धो महाराज नकुलः परवीरहा । क्षुरप्रेण सुतीक्ष्णेन कर्णस्य धनुरच्छिनत् ॥
data.md: Thereupon, O mighty king, the highly enraged Nakula, that slayer of heroic foes, severed the bow of Karna with sharp razor-like arrows.

data.v: अथैनं छिन्नधन्वानं सायकानां शतैस्त्रिभिः । आजघ्ने प्रहसन्वीरः सर्वलोकमहारथम् ॥
data.md: Thereupon that brave warrior (the son of Pandu) smilingly struck this one (Karna), the mightiest of all car-warriors, (Karma) whose bow severed with three hundred shafts.

data.v: कर्णमभ्यर्दितं दृष्ट्वा पाण्डुपुत्रेण मारिष । विस्मयं परमं जग्मू रथिनः सह दैवतैः ॥
data.md: O sire, seeing, Karna thus crushed by the son of Pandu, all the car-warriors, along with the celestials, obtained the highest condition of astonishment.

data.v: अथान्यद्धनुरादाय कर्णो वैकर्तनस्तदा । नकुलं पञ्चभिर्बाणैर्जत्रुदेशे समार्दयत् ॥
data.md: Then Karna, the son of Vikartana, grasping another bow, had shot upon Nakula five shafts in the shoulder-joint.

data.v: उरःस्थैरथ तैर्बाणैर्माद्रीपुत्रो व्यरोचत । स्वरश्मिभिरिवादित्यो भुवने विसृजन्प्रभाम् ॥
data.md: Thus the son of Madri blazed with those arrows sticking to that place (in his body); even as the sun, shedding lustre on the earth, looks resplendent with his own rays.

data.v: नकुलस्तु ततः कर्णं विद्ध्वा सप्तभिरायसैः । अथास्य धनुषः कोटिं पुनश्चिच्छेद मारिष ॥
data.md: Thereupon Nakula, indeed, after having penetrated Karna with seven impetuous arrows, once more severed one of the horns of his bow, O sire.

data.v: सोऽन्यत्कार्मुकमादाय समरे वेगवत्तरम् । नकुलस्य ततो बाणैः सर्वतोऽवारयद्दिशः ॥
data.md: Thereupon in the field of battle he (Karna), taking up another bow, that was possessed of greater strength, closed the different points of the compass, on every side of Nakula, with his arrows.

data.v: संछाद्यमानः सहसा कर्णचापच्युतैः शरैः । चिच्छेद स शरांस्तूर्णं शरैरेव महारथः ॥
data.md: That mighty car-warrior (Nakula), being thus suddenly closed with the arrows, shot from Karna's bow, rapidly struck down these shafts with the arrows of his own.

data.v: ततो बाणमयं जालं विततं व्योम्न्यदृश्यत । खद्योतानां गणैरेव संपतद्भिर्यथा नभः ॥
data.md: Then that net-work of arrows, spread over the sky, looked like the firmament, covered over with innumerable fire-flies, that roved about it.

data.v: तैर्विमुक्तैः शरशतैश्छादितं गगनं तदा । शलभानां यथा व्रातैस्तद्वदासीत्समाकुलम् ॥
data.md: Then, O ruler of earth, the welkin, covered over as it was with the hundreds of arrows shot by both of them, looked even as it was covered over with the swarms of locusts,

data.v: ते शरा हेमविकृताः संपतन्तो मुहुर्मुहुः । श्रेणीकृता अभासन्त हंसाः श्रेणीगता इव ॥
data.md: Those arrows, that were adorned with gold, having issued forth in continuous lines, looked most handsome like the cranes flying in continuous lines (through the sky).

data.v: बाणजालावृते व्योम्नि छादिते च दिवाकरे । समसर्पत्ततो भूतं किंचिदेव विशां पते ॥
data.md: When the firmament was thus closed with the net-work of arrows and the sun was covered over with them, none of the rovers of the sky descended upon the earth.

data.v: निरुद्धे तत्र मार्गे तु शरसंघैः समन्ततः । व्यरोचतां महाभागौ बालसूर्याविवोदितौ ॥
data.md: While all the directions were thus closed with the shots of innumerable arrows from all sides, those two lofty-minded heroes blazed forth like two risen suns appearing at the time of universals dissolution,

data.v: कर्णचापच्युतैर्बाणैर्वध्यमानास्तु सोमकाः । अवालीयन्त राजेन्द्र वेदनार्ताः शरार्दिताः ॥
data.md: O foremost of monarchs, having been highly oppressed with the pain and greatly crushed and slaughtered by these arrows shot from the bow of Karna, all the Somakas dicd.

data.v: नकुलस्य तथा बाणैर्वध्यमाना चमूस्तव । व्यशीर्यत दिशो राजन्वातनुन्ना इवाम्बुदाः ॥
data.md: In the same way, O king, the army on your side, thus slain by the arrows of Nakuſa, dispersed on all sides; even as the masses of clouds are dispersed by the wind.

data.v: ते सेने वध्यमाने तु ताभ्यां दिव्यैर्महाशरैः । शरपातमपक्रम्य ततः प्रेक्षकवत्स्थिते ॥
data.md: The two armies, being thus slaughtered by both the (above) warriors with divine arrows, possessed of great impetuosity, fled beyond the WW reach of falling shafts and stood even as they were spectators (of the battle).

data.v: प्रोत्सारिते जने तस्मिन्कर्णपाण्डवयोः शरैः । विव्याधाते महात्मानावन्योन्यं शरवृष्टिभिः ॥
data.md: Thus when both the armies were dispersed by the arrows of Karna and the son of Pandu, these two high-minded warriors pierced each other with showers of shafts.

data.v: निदर्शयन्तौ त्वस्त्राणि दिव्यानि रणमूर्धनि । छादयन्तौ च सहसा परस्परवधैषिणौ ॥
data.md: Most willing to kill each other, both the warriors showed their celestial weapons in the battle-field and closed each other all on a sudden (with showers of arrows).

data.v: नकुलेन शरा मुक्ताः कङ्कबर्हिणवाससः । ते तु कर्णमवच्छाद्य व्यतिष्ठन्त यथा परे ॥
data.md: The arrows that were furnished with the Kanka, the peacock feathers and garments, shot by Nakula, after having closed the son of Suta, appeared to stay on the sky.

data.v: शरवेश्मप्रविष्टौ तौ ददृशाते न कैश्चन । चन्द्रसूर्यौ यथा राजंश्छाद्यमानौ जलागमे ॥
data.md: O monarch, both the warriors, having entered the chambers composed of arrows, could not be seen by any persons; even as both the sun and the moon, covered over with the masses of clouds, cannot be seen by any persons.

data.v: ततः क्रुद्धो रणे कर्णः कृत्वा घोरतरं वपुः । पाण्डवं छादयामास समन्ताच्छरवृष्टिभिः ॥
data.md: Thereupon Karna, who was highly enraged, after having assumed a very terrible look in the field of battle, shrouded the son of Pandu with showers of shafts shot from all sides,

data.v: स च्छाद्यमानः समरे सूतपुत्रेण पाण्डवः । न चकार व्यथां राजन्भास्करो जलदैर्यथा ॥
data.md: O powerful monarch, the son Pandu, who was wholly shrouded by the son of Suta (with arrowy showers), did not feel any uneasiness; even as the sun (the giver of light), covered by the clouds, feels no pain.

data.v: ततः प्रहस्याधिरथिः शरजालानि मारिष । प्रेषयामास समरे शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥
data.md: Thereupon, O sire, the son of Adhiratha, after smiling from a time, shot forth hundreds and thousands of shafts in the field of battle.

data.v: एकच्छायमभूत्सर्वं तस्य बाणैर्महात्मनः । अभ्रच्छायेव संजज्ञे संपतद्भिः शरोत्तमैः ॥
data.md: There (upon the field of battle) all appeared to be one continuous shade by the shafts of that lofty-minded one (Karna) even as there formed a shade of clouds by the foremost of falling arrows.

data.v: ततः कर्णो महाराज धनुश्छित्त्वा महात्मनः । सारथिं पातयामास रथनीडाद्धसन्निव ॥
data.md: Then, O powerful monarch, Karna after having severed the bow of that high-souled one (Nakula), smilingly caused the fall of his charioteer from the car-nichi.

data.v: तथाश्वांश्चतुरश्चास्य चतुर्भिर्निशितैः शरैः । यमस्य सदनं तूर्णं प्रेषयामास भारत ॥
data.md: Thereupon, O descendant of the Bharata race, he (Karna) sent away the four horses of him (Nakula) to the abode of Death most rapidly by means of four sharp-edged arrows.

data.v: अथास्य तं रथं तूर्णं तिलशो व्यधमच्छरैः । पताकां चक्ररक्षौ च ध्वजं खड्गं च मारिष । शतचन्द्रं ततश्चर्म सर्वोपकरणानि च ॥
data.md: Then also he with innumerable arrows, cutoff into minute fragments his (antagonist's) celestial car, his standard, the protector of his car-wheels, his mace and sword and his shield, that was furnished with hundreds of moons, as well as his all other equipment's of war, O sire.

data.v: हताश्वो विरथश्चैव विवर्मा च विशां पते । अवतीर्य रथात्तूर्णं परिघं गृह्य विष्ठितः ॥
data.md: O ruler of earth, losing his horse and being deprived of his car and shield, he (Nakula) immediately alighted from his car and taking up his spiked club, stood (in the field of battle).

data.v: तमुद्यतं महाघोरं परिघं तस्य सूतजः । व्यहनत्सायकै राजञ्शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥
data.md: O monarch, the son of Suta had struck down that dreadful mace, uplifted by him, with the keenest arrows, capable of bearing the greatest strain.

data.v: व्यायुधं चैनमालक्ष्य शरैः संनतपर्वभिः । आर्दयद्बहुशः कर्णो न चैनं समपीडयत् ॥
data.md: On seeing him (his antagonist) without any weapons, Karna afflicted him with numerous straight arrows; but he did not oppress him too severely.

data.v: स वध्यमानः समरे कृतास्त्रेण बलीयसा । प्राद्रवत्सहसा राजन्नकुलो व्याकुलेन्द्रियः ॥
data.md: O monarch, Nakula of agitated senses, who was struck by that most powerful warrior, well versed in the science of arms in the battle, fled away all on a sudden.

data.v: तमभिद्रुत्य राधेयः प्रहसन्वै पुनः पुनः । सज्यमस्य धनुः कण्ठे सोऽवासृजत भारत ॥
data.md: O descendant of the Bharata race, the sons of Radha, indeed laughing, again and again and pursuing him (Nakula), placed the bow, that was furnished with string, around his neck.

data.v: ततः स शुशुभे राजन्कण्ठासक्तमहाधनुः । परिवेषमनुप्राप्तो यथा स्याद्व्योम्नि चन्द्रमाः । यथैव च सितो मेघः शक्रचापेन शोभितः ॥
data.md: Thereupon, O king, that strong bow placed round his neck, blazed forth, like the moon in the firmament, when he is surrounded by a halo of light or like the mass of black clouds adorned by the bow Indra.

data.v: तमब्रवीत्तदा कर्णो व्यर्थं व्याहृतवानसि । वदेदानीं पुनर्हृष्टो वध्यं मां त्वं पुनः पुनः ॥
मा योत्सीर्गुरुभिः सार्धं बलवद्भिश्च पाण्डव । सदृशैस्तात युध्यस्व व्रीडां मा कुरु पाण्डव । गृहं वा गच्छ माद्रेय यत्र वा कृष्णफल्गुनौ ॥
data.md: Then Karna addressed him thus-'whatever you speak is of no avail. Being delighted, do you utter those words once more, as you are struck over and over again. O son of Pandu, do you not fight with the mightiest of Kurus; O son, fight with those, that are your cquals. O son of Pandu, do not be ashamed of it. O son of Madri, go home, where are Krishna and Falguna.' O most powerful monarch, he then, having addressed him thus, dismissed him at that time.

data.v: एवमुक्त्वा महाराज व्यसर्जयत तं ततः । वधप्राप्तं तु तं राजन्नावधीत्सूतनन्दनः । स्मृत्वा कुन्त्या वचो राजंस्तत एनं व्यसर्जयत् ॥
data.md: Thereupon that hero (Karna), who was well-versed in the code of morality and did not slaughter him (Nakula), who was almost within the reach of Death himself. Then, O monarch, resembling the words of Kunti, he (Karna) let hiin go.

data.v: विसृष्टः पाण्डवो राजन्सूतपुत्रेण धन्विना । व्रीडन्निव जगामाथ युधिष्ठिररथं प्रति ॥
data.md: O king, the son of Pandu, being thus abandoned by that bowman, the son of Suta and feeling shame for it, went towards the car of Yudhishthira.

data.v: आरुरोह रथं चापि सूतपुत्रप्रतापितः । निःश्वसन्दुःखसंतप्तः कुम्भे क्षिप्त इवोरगः ॥
data.md: He then, being afflicted by the son of Suta, ascended the car (of his brother) and being oppressed with grief, sighed heavily like shake confided within a vessel.

data.v: तं विसृज्य रणे कर्णः पाञ्चालांस्त्वरितो ययौ । रथेनातिपताकेन चन्द्रवर्णहयेन च ॥
data.md: Then Karna, after having defeated him (Nakula), rushed most rapidly against the Panchalas, riding upon a car, that was furnished with innumerable standards and having the colour of the moon.

data.v: तत्राक्रन्दो महानासीत्पाण्डवानां विशां पते । दृष्ट्वा सेनापतिं यान्तं पाञ्चालानां रथव्रजान् ॥
data.md: On seeing the commander of the (Kaurava) army rushing against the car-warriors of the Panchala force, there arose a dreadful uproar against the Pandavas, O ruler of earth.

data.v: तत्राकरोन्महाराज कदनं सूतनन्दनः । मध्यं गते दिनकरे चक्रवत्प्रचरन्प्रभुः ॥
data.md: O most powerful monarch, that lord the son of Suta, circling round the field of battle, like a wheel, perpetuated an immense slaughter there at the time when the sun attained the meridian.

data.v: भग्नचक्रै रथैः केचिच्छिन्नध्वजपताकिभिः । ससूतैर्हतसूतैश्च भग्नाक्षैश्चैव मारिष । ह्रियमाणानपश्याम पाञ्चालानां रथव्रजान् ॥
data.md: O sire, we saw numerous car-warriors of the Panchala army, who were carried away (from the field of battle) upon cars, some of which had their, wheels broken down and some of which had their banners and standards torn into pieces and some also had their horses and drivers slaughtered (in the battle) and some, again, were without their wheels,

data.v: तत्र तत्र च संभ्रान्ता विचेरुर्मत्तकुञ्जराः । दवाग्निना परीताङ्गा यथैव स्युर्महावने ॥
data.md: Innumerable elephants, also wandered and run about in the different directions of the field of battle, some of which had their bodies wholly burnt by the forest-fire.

data.v: भिन्नकुम्भा विरुधिराश्छिन्नहस्ताश्च वारणाः । भिन्नगात्रवराश्चैव च्छिन्नवालाश्च मारिष । छिन्नाभ्राणीव संपेतुर्वध्यमाना महात्मना ॥
data.md: Innumerable elephants had their frontal globes severed and the bodies besmeared with blood and the trunks cut-off into fragments. Moreover, O sire, some other elephants, being slaughtered by that high souled one (Karna) fell down with their armour cut-off, or their tails curtailed, like the masses of clouds dispersed by the wind.

data.v: अपरे त्रासिता नागा नाराचशततोमरैः । तमेवाभिमुखा यान्ति शलभा इव पावकम् ॥
data.md: Again, other elephants, that were terrified by the shots of arrows and lances of sons of Radha, rushed with their faces towards him (the son of Radha); even as the insects rush towards the blazing fire.

data.v: अपरे निष्टनन्तः स्म व्यदृश्यन्त महाद्विपाः । क्षरन्तः शोणितं गात्रैर्नगा इव जलप्लवम् ॥
data.md: Other mighty elephants were looked to strike against one another. They also shed blood from their limbs, even as the mountains let flow streams of water from their summits.

data.v: उरश्छदैर्विमुक्ताश्च वालबन्धैश्च वाजिनः । राजतैश्च तथा कांस्यैः सौवर्णैश्चैव भूषणैः ॥
हीना आस्तरणैश्चैव खलीनैश्च विवर्जिताः । चामरैश्च कुथाभिश्च तूणीरैः पतितैरपि ॥
निहतैः सादिभिश्चैव शूरैराहवशोभिभिः । अपश्याम रणे तत्र भ्राम्यमाणान्हयोत्तमान् ॥
प्रासैः खड्गैश्च संस्यूतानृष्टिभिश्च नराधिप । हययोधानपश्याम कञ्चुकोष्णीषधारिणः ॥

data.md: We behold the cars, that were adorned with gold and to which were yoked the heroes of greatest speed, dragged in the different directions of the field with great rapidity; while their riders were all slaughtered.

data.md: O descendant of the Bharata race, some of these cars had their axes and poles shattered into fragments; and some others had their wheels broken; and others, again had their banners and standards torn into pieces; and several others were deprived of their arrows.

data.v: विहीनान्रथिनस्तत्र धावमानान्समन्ततः । सूर्यपुत्रशरैस्त्रस्तानपश्याम विशां पते ॥

data.md: We saw numerous elephants running in all directions of the field of battle, that were adorned with innumerable stars and that were furnished with the most handsome bells and also that were ornamented with banners variegated with various colours.

data.v: शिरांसि बाहूनूरूंश्च छिन्नानन्यांस्तथा युधि । कर्णचापच्युतैर्बाणैरपश्याम विनाकृतान् ॥
data.md: Moreover, we behold on all side of the field of battle, numerous heads, arms, chests and other parts of the body, that were severed by the arrows shot from the bow of Karna.

data.v: महान्व्यतिकरो रौद्रो योधानामन्वदृश्यत । कर्णसायकनुन्नानां हतानां निशितैः शरैः ॥
data.md: The most dreadful and distressing calamity had fallen upon all the warriors while they were fighting with the keen arrows and cut-off with the shafts of Karna.

data.v: ते वध्यमानाः समरे सूतपुत्रेण सृञ्जयाः । तमेवाभिमुखा यान्ति पतंगा इव पावकम् ॥
data.md: The Srinjayas were slaughtered by the son of Suta in the field of battle and they rushed towards the force of Karna, even as the insects rash towards the fire.

data.v: तं दहन्तमनीकानि तत्र तत्र महारथम् । क्षत्रिया वर्जयामासुर्युगान्ताग्निमिवोल्बणम् ॥
data.md: All the Kshatriyas (the warriors) abandoned that mighty car-warrior who was slaughtering the forces (belonging to the Pandavas) on all sides of the battle, even as they abandon the blazing fire, that appears at the universal dissolution.

data.v: हतशेषास्तु ये वीराः पाञ्चालानां महारथाः । तान्प्रभग्नान्द्रुतान्कर्णः पृष्ठतो विकिरञ्शरैः । अभ्यधावत तेजस्वी विशीर्णकवचध्वजान् ॥
data.md: That hero of immense prowess (Karna) pursued these powerful car-warriors belonging to the Panchala divisions, shooting dreadful arrows at them from behind, while they (these car-warriors), as they survived the slaughter, were broken and running away from the field and deprived of their armours and standards. The son of Suta, who was endowed with great strength, afflicted them with his arrows; even as the remover of darkness (the sun), having reached the meridian, afflicts all the creatures with his rays.

data.v: तापयामास तान्बाणैः सूतपुत्रो महारथः । मध्यंदिनमनुप्राप्तो भूतानीव तमोनुदः ॥
युयुत्सुं तव पुत्रं तु प्राद्रवन्तं महद्बलम् । उलूकोऽभ्यपतत्तूर्णं तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत् ॥
data.md: Sanjaya said Then Uluka rushed most rapidly against Yuyutsu, who was routing the vast force belonging to your son; and uttered to him those words-'do you wait, do you wait.'

data.v: युयुत्सुस्तु ततो राजञ्शितधारेण पत्रिणा । उलूकं ताडयामास वज्रेणेन्द्र इवाचलम् ॥
data.md: Thereupon, O monarch, Yuyutsu afflicted Uluka with a sharp-edged arrow (supplied with wings), even as a huge mountain is struck with the thunderbolt.

data.v: उलूकस्तु ततः क्रुद्धस्तव पुत्रस्य संयुगे । क्षुरप्रेण धनुश्छित्त्वा ताडयामास कर्णिना ॥
data.md: Thus Uluka, too, being highly enraged and cutting off the bow of your son with a razor like shaft, struck him with a barbed arrows in the field of battle.

data.v: तदपास्य धनुश्छिन्नं युयुत्सुर्वेगवत्तरम् । अन्यदादत्त सुमहच्चापं संरक्तलोचनः ॥
data.md: Yuyutsu, whose eyes became red with anger, after having thrown aside that severed bow, grasped another, the most dreadful one, possessed of greater impetuosity.

data.v: शाकुनिं च ततः षष्ट्या विव्याध भरतर्षभ । सारथिं त्रिभिरानर्छत्तं च भूयो व्यविध्यत ॥
data.md: Thereupon, O foremost of the Bharata race, he (Yuyutsu) penetrated Uluka with sixty arrows; and then struck down his driver with three; and he once more pierced him (Uluka).

data.v: उलूकस्तं तु विंशत्या विद्ध्वा हेमविभूषितैः । अथास्य समरे क्रुद्धो ध्वजं चिच्छेद काञ्चनम् ॥
data.md: Uluka, too, who became highly wrathful, after having pierced him (Yuyutsu) with twenty arrows, decked with gold, struck down his standards, that was made of gold, in the field of battle.

data.v: स च्छिन्नयष्टिः सुमहाञ्शीर्यमाणो महाध्वजः । पपात प्रमुखे राजन्युयुत्सोः काञ्चनोज्ज्वलः ॥
data.md: O monarch, that huge and magnificent standard, that one made of gold, being torn off and shattered into fragments, dropped down in front of Yuyutsu.

data.v: ध्वजमुन्मथितं दृष्ट्वा युयुत्सुः क्रोधमूर्छितः । उलूकं पञ्चभिर्बाणैराजघान स्तनान्तरे ॥
data.md: Seeing his standards thus cut-off, Yuyutsu, who became senseless with rage, struck Uluka with five arrows in the chest.

data.v: उलूकस्तस्य भल्लेन तैलधौतेन मारिष । शिरश्चिच्छेद सहसा यन्तुर्भरतसत्तम ॥
data.md: O descendant of the Bharata race, O sire, Uluka then severed the head of his foe, with a broad-headed arrows, dipped in oil, in the field of battle.

data.v: जघान चतुरोऽश्वांश्च तं च विव्याध पञ्चभिः । सोऽतिविद्धो बलवता प्रत्यपायाद्रथान्तरम् ॥
data.md: Then he (Uluka), slaughtered his four horses and pierced himself (Yuyutsu) with five shafts. He (Yuyutsu), being thus fierced by that powerful one (Uluka) went into another car.

data.v: तं निर्जित्य रणे राजन्नुलूकस्त्वरितो ययौ । पाञ्चालान्सृञ्जयांश्चैव विनिघ्नन्निशितैः शरैः ॥
data.md: O monarch, Uluka, after having defeated him (his antagonist) in the battle, hastened towards the Panchalas and the Srinjayas and slew them with the keen arrows.

data.v: शतानीकं महाराज श्रुतकर्मा सुतस्तव । व्यश्वसूतरथं चक्रे निमेषार्धादसंभ्रमम् ॥
data.md: O mighty monarch, your son, Srutakarman, deprived, without any fear, Shatanika of his horses, charioteer and car within half the time taken up by the twinkling on an eye.

data.md: O sire, that mighty car-warrior, Shatanika, waiting in a car, that was deprived of its horses and becoming very wrathful, had thrown a mace upon your son.

data.v: सा कृत्वा स्यन्दनं भस्म हयांश्चैव ससारथीन् । पपात धरणीं तूर्णं दारयन्तीव भारत ॥
data.md: O descendant of the Bharata race, that mace, after having reduced the car and the horses along with the riders themselves into dusts (belonging to your son), fell down upon the earth most rapidly and penetrated through it.

data.v: तावुभौ विरथौ वीरौ कुरूणां कीर्तिवर्धनौ । अपाक्रमेतां युद्धार्तौ प्रेक्षमाणौ परस्परम् ॥
data.md: Then those two brave warriors, who were divested of their cars and who also had contributed to the increase of the glory of the Kurus, really fled away from the battle, looking each other in the face.

data.v: पुत्रस्तु तव संभ्रान्तो विवित्सो रथमाविशत् । शतानीकोऽपि त्वरितः प्रतिविन्ध्यरथं गतः ॥
data.md: Thereupon your son, who became highly terrified, ascended the ascended the car of Vivingsa. Shatanika, too, with rapidity, mounted upon the car of Prativindhya.

data.v: सुतसोमस्तु शकुनिं विव्याध निशितैः शरैः । नाकम्पयत संरब्धो वार्योघ इव पर्वतम् ॥
data.md: Shakuni, who became very angry after having pierced Sutasoma with excellently sharpened arrows, could not cause him to tremble (with fear); even as a torrent of rain cannot shake a mountain.

data.md: O descendant of the Bharata race, Sutasoma, too, after having seen the bitterest enemy of his father, closed him with several thousands of arrows.

data.md: Shakuni, too, on the other hand, who was of light arms and who was acquainted with all sorts of warfare and who, again, was most desirous of winning victory, severed all those shafts with other winged arrows of his own. data.v: निवार्य समरे चापि शरांस्तान्निशितैः शरैः । आजघान सुसंक्रुद्धः सुतसोमं त्रिभिः शरैः ॥
data.md: Shakuni, too, on the other hand, who was of light arms and who was acquainted with all sorts of warfare and who, again, was most desirous of winning victory, severed all those shafts with other winged arrows of his own. data.v: तस्याश्वान्केतनं सूतं तिलशो व्यधमच्छरैः । स्यालस्तव महावीर्यस्ततस्ते चुक्रुशुर्जनाः ॥
data.md: Thereupon, O great king, your brother-inlaw cut of his (antagonist's) horses, standard and charioteer into minute pieces by numerous arrows. At this, the people sent forth a loud roar.

data.v: हताश्वो विरथश्चैव छिन्नधन्वा च मारिष । धन्वी धनुर्वरं गृह्य रथाद्भूमावतिष्ठत । व्यसृजत्सायकांश्चैव स्वर्णपुङ्खाञ्शिलाशितान् ॥
data.md: O sire, after taken up another excellent bow, that great bowman who was now steedless and carless and whose standard and charioteer into minute pieces by numerous arrows. At this, the people sent forth a loud roar.

data.v: छादयामासुरथ ते तव स्यालस्य तं रथम् । पतंगानामिव व्राताः शरव्राता महारथम् ॥

data.md: That mighty car-warrior, the son of Subala did not at all feel pain to behold the fights of arrows, that were like the throngs of locusts, approaching towards his car. Rather that highly glorious one really restrained those arrows with numcrous arrows of his own.

data.v: तत्रातुष्यन्त योधाश्च सिद्धाश्चापि दिवि स्थिताः । सुतसोमस्य तत्कर्म दृष्ट्वाश्रद्धेयमद्भुतम् । रथस्थं नृपतिं तं तु पदातिः सन्नयोधयत् ॥
data.md: There (in the field of battle) the warriors, as well as the Siddhas resting in the firmament, became highly gratificd to witness that extraordinary and incredible deed of Sutasoma. For he (Sutasoma) was fighting on foot with Shakuni, who rested upon his car.

data.v: तस्य तीक्ष्णैर्महावेगैर्भल्लैः संनतपर्वभिः । व्यहनत्कार्मुकं राजा तूणीरं चैव सर्वशः ॥
data.md: O king, he (Shakuni) severed the bow, as well as all the quivers of him (Sutasoma) by means of his broad-headed arrows, that were excellently whetted and also that were endued with great impetuosity and again, that were very straight. was
